item.content:encoded:
The UN Maps Learning Hub provides an online self-training platform for people who want to learn how open geospatial information can support United Nations development and peacekeeping efforts. The platform, offered through UN Mappers, brings together a series of online courses covering essential and advanced geospatial skills, including OpenStreetMap editing, QGIS analysis, map making, and the use of the UN Maps application. Designed for people discovering open geospatial information as well as learners who want to develop more advanced technical skills, the UN Maps Learning Hub provides an accessible way to study geospatial tools and techniques online. Learners can enroll in available courses, monitor their progress, and complete quizzes and tests as they work through individual sections or entire courses. The platform also benefits from an active UN Mappers community that can help newcomers connect with experienced contributors when they have questions. There is no application deadline stated in the information provided. Since the platform is described as a self-training resource, learners can explore the available courses according to their own learning needs and schedule, subject to any course-specific requirements.

What Is the UN Maps Learning Hub?

The UN Maps Learning Hub is an online learning platform created to help people develop knowledge and practical skills in open geospatial information.

Its focus is closely connected to the work of the United Nations, particularly the use of geospatial information in support of development and peacekeeping.

Geospatial information is information that has a geographic or location-based component. It can be used to understand places, map features, analyze geographic patterns, and support decision-making.

The Learning Hub provides training in several tools and areas that are important to open geospatial work, including:

  • OpenStreetMap editing
  • QGIS analysis
  • Map making
  • UN Maps application
  • Basic geospatial techniques
  • Advanced geospatial techniques

Rather than being limited to one course or one specific skill level, the platform contains a series of courses designed to help learners develop their understanding progressively.What Can You Learn Through the UN Maps Learning Hub?

The platform focuses on practical open geospatial information and provides courses covering both foundational and more advanced concepts.

1. OpenStreetMap Editing

One of the major areas covered by the Learning Hub is OpenStreetMap editing.

OpenStreetMap is an open mapping platform where geographic information can be created, edited, and improved by contributors.

The UN Maps Learning Hub includes training designed to help learners understand basic and advanced features of OpenStreetMap editing.

This can be particularly useful for people interested in learning how geographic information can be created and maintained collaboratively.

Learners can develop their knowledge of OpenStreetMap editing while understanding how open geospatial information can contribute to humanitarian, development, and peacekeeping-related activities.

2. QGIS Analysis

The Learning Hub also provides training related to QGIS analysis.

QGIS is a geographic information system used to work with spatial and geographic information.

Through the available training, learners can develop skills related to analyzing geospatial information and working with geographic datasets.

The inclusion of both basic and advanced geospatial training makes the platform relevant to learners who are at different stages of their geospatial learning journey.

3. Map Making

Another area covered by the Learning Hub is map making.

Maps are an important way of presenting geographic information in a form that can be interpreted and communicated.

The courses can help learners develop knowledge of creating maps and working with geospatial information in ways that support the presentation of geographic data.

For learners interested in cartography, GIS, humanitarian mapping, development work, or peacekeeping applications, map-making skills can provide an important foundation for working with geographic information.

4. Using the UN Maps Application

The Learning Hub also provides training on how to leverage the UN Maps application.

This makes the platform particularly relevant to people who want to understand how UN Maps can be used alongside open geospatial information.

Rather than focusing exclusively on general GIS concepts, the platform connects its training to the broader objective of supporting United Nations development and peacekeeping efforts.

Learn more and apply  HERE

Who Can Use the UN Maps Learning Hub?

The platform is described as a self-training platform accessible to anyone discovering open geospatial information to support United Nations development and peacekeeping efforts.

This means the opportunity is not presented as being restricted to applicants from a particular country, continent, or nationality.

The provided information does not specify requirements such as:

  • A university degree
  • A particular academic discipline
  • A minimum age
  • A specific nationality
  • A particular race or ethnicity
  • Previous professional experience
  • A specific level of GIS knowledge

Instead, the platform is presented as a learning resource that people can use to develop their knowledge of open geospatial information.

However, learners should pay attention to individual course restrictions because the platform states that some courses are reserved for UN personnel only.

Multilingual Learning Platform

A significant feature of the UN Maps Learning Hub is its multilingual approach.

According to the provided information, the platform supports the six official languages of the United Nations, with the text specifically identifying:

  • Arabic
  • Chinese
  • English
  • French
  • Russian

It also states that other languages are available through community-led translation.

This multilingual approach can make the learning platform more accessible to people from different linguistic backgrounds and communities.

The community-led translation component also reflects the collaborative nature of open geospatial work, where contributors can help make resources available to a wider audience.

Study Online and Learn at Your Own Pace

The UN Maps Learning Hub is designed for online study.

Learners can enroll in courses and track their progress as they work through the material.

The platform incorporates:

  • Courses
  • Individual sections
  • Quizzes
  • Tests
  • Progress tracking

Learners can therefore use assessments to check their understanding while progressing through the course material. The platform allows learners to track their progress through quizzes and tests either for individual sections or the entire course. This structure can be useful for learners who want to approach geospatial training systematically rather than simply reading standalone resources.

Community Support for Learners

Learning a technical subject can sometimes be challenging, particularly for people who are encountering geospatial tools for the first time. The UN Maps Learning Hub addresses this through access to the UN Mappers community. According to the provided information, the UN Mappers community is available to help newcomers.

Learners who have questions can reach out through:

  • Email
  • Social media

The community can then connect learners with expert contributors who may be able to help answer their questions. This community-support component provides an additional learning resource beyond the courses themselves.

Why Learn Open Geospatial Information?

Open geospatial information can be an important resource for understanding locations, mapping geographic features, analyzing spatial information, and supporting decisions. The UN Maps Learning Hub specifically places these skills in the context of United Nations development and peacekeeping efforts.

For someone interested in developing geospatial knowledge, learning these tools can provide exposure to several complementary areas:

  1. Open mapping through OpenStreetMap.
  2. Geospatial analysis through QGIS.
  3. Cartography and map making.
  4. UN Maps and its applications.
  5. Online assessment and progress tracking.
  6. Community-based learning and expert support.

The combination means learners can explore both the technical side of geospatial information and its potential applications in a United Nations context.

What Makes the UN Maps Learning Hub Different?

One of the key characteristics of the platform is that it brings several aspects of geospatial learning together.

Instead of focusing exclusively on one software tool, it covers:

  • OpenStreetMap
  • QGIS
  • Map making
  • UN Maps

It also combines structured online courses with quizzes, tests, progress tracking, multilingual resources, and community support.

This makes the Learning Hub a potentially useful starting point for someone who is new to open geospatial information as well as a resource for learners seeking to develop more advanced skills.

Is the UN Maps Learning Hub Free?

The information provided describes the platform as a self-training platform accessible to anyone, but it does not explicitly state a tuition fee or provide a detailed pricing structure.

Therefore, the provided information does not explicitly confirm a separate fee-free policy for every course.

Learners should check the platform and individual course information for any applicable requirements or restrictions.

Are There Any Application Deadlines?

No application deadline is provided in the information supplied.

The UN Maps Learning Hub is presented as an online self-training platform rather than a conventional competitive application program.

However, individual courses could have their own conditions or restrictions, so learners should review the information associated with the specific course they want to take.

Some Courses Are Reserved for UN Personnel

Although the Learning Hub is broadly accessible, an important restriction should not be overlooked.

The platform states that some courses are reserved for UN personnel only.

Therefore, prospective learners should distinguish between:

  • Courses available to the wider public, and
  • Courses specifically restricted to UN personnel.

Being able to access the Learning Hub does not necessarily mean that every course on the platform is available to every learner.

How to Get Started With the UN Maps Learning Hub

People interested in developing their open geospatial skills can begin by exploring the available courses on the platform.

A practical approach would be to:

Step 1: Explore the available courses

Review the courses offered through the Learning Hub and identify those that match your interests and current skill level.

Step 2: Start with foundational material

If you are new to geospatial information, begin with introductory content before moving into more advanced features.

Step 3: Develop OpenStreetMap skills

Explore the training covering basic and advanced OpenStreetMap editing.

Step 4: Learn QGIS

Use the relevant courses to develop your understanding of QGIS analysis.

Step 5: Practice map making

Build your knowledge of creating and presenting maps using geospatial information.

Step 6: Explore UN Maps

Learn how the UN Maps application can be leveraged in connection with open geospatial information.

Step 7: Complete quizzes and tests

Use the platform’s quizzes and tests to check your understanding and monitor your progress.

Step 8: Use community support

If you encounter difficulties, contact the UN Mappers community through the available communication channels and seek assistance from expert contributors.

Who Could Benefit From This Online Learning Opportunity?

Although the platform does not specify a particular professional or academic background for general access, its subject matter could be relevant to people interested in areas such as:

  • Open mapping
  • Geographic information systems
  • Geospatial analysis
  • Cartography
  • Map making
  • Humanitarian mapping
  • Development-related mapping
  • Peacekeeping-related geospatial work
  • OpenStreetMap
  • QGIS
  • United Nations-related geospatial applications
  • Geographic data
  • Spatial analysis

The platform may also be useful for learners who simply want to discover open geospatial information and understand how it can support development and peacekeeping activities.

Key Features of the UN Maps Learning Hub

Feature Details
Platform UN Maps Learning Hub
Organization UN Mappers
Format Online self-training
Accessibility Accessible to anyone discovering open geospatial information, subject to course restrictions
Main focus Open geospatial information
OpenStreetMap Basic and advanced editing
QGIS Geospatial analysis
Map making Included
UN Maps Training on leveraging the application
Languages Six UN official languages are stated as supported, plus community-translated languages
Assessments Quizzes and tests
Progress tracking Available
Community support UN Mappers community and expert contributors
Restricted courses Some courses are reserved for UN personnel
Deadline No deadline stated in the provided information
Location Online

Important Things to Know Before You Start

Before beginning your learning journey, keep these points in mind:

  • The platform is focused on open geospatial information.
  • Training covers both basic and advanced features.
  • OpenStreetMap and QGIS are two major areas of study.
  • Map making is also included.
  • The platform provides training on the UN Maps application.
  • Courses can be completed online.
  • Learners can track their progress.
  • Quizzes and tests are incorporated into the learning process.
  • The platform supports multiple languages.
  • Community-led translation provides additional language accessibility.
  • The UN Mappers community provides support to newcomers.
  • Some courses are restricted to UN personnel.
  • No application deadline is specified in the supplied information.

Conclusion

The UN Maps Learning Hub is an online self-training platform designed to introduce and develop knowledge of open geospatial information in support of United Nations development and peacekeeping efforts.

Through its collection of courses, learners can explore important geospatial skills including OpenStreetMap editing, QGIS analysis, map making, and the use of the UN Maps application. The platform accommodates different stages of learning by offering both basic and advanced features while allowing participants to track their progress through quizzes and tests.

Another important strength of the Learning Hub is its multilingual and community-oriented approach. The platform supports multiple languages, including the United Nations’ official languages as stated in the provided information, while community-led translation helps extend access to additional languages. Learners can also connect with the UN Mappers community and seek assistance from expert contributors when they encounter questions or difficulties.

The platform is broadly accessible to people interested in discovering open geospatial information, although some individual courses are reserved for UN personnel. No specific nationality, race, country, continent, academic degree, or professional qualification is identified as a general requirement in the supplied information.

For anyone looking to build knowledge of OpenStreetMap, QGIS, digital mapping, geospatial analysis, and UN Maps, the UN Maps Learning Hub offers an opportunity to learn online and develop practical familiarity with tools and concepts that support geographic information work.

For more opportunities click HERE

item.content:encoded:
DW Akademie has published a varied set of 2026 opportunities for media professionals, trainers, consultants, service providers and young participants. The current calls span Africa, Asia, Syria, the Western Balkans and Germany, with assignments focused on digital safety, artificial intelligence, journalism training, podcast production, cultural programming, media and information literacy, and institutional resilience.

The official DW Akademie opportunities and tenders page currently includes both actionable calls and listings whose deadlines have recently passed. For clarity, this article first explains the six opportunities that remained open or actionable on August 31, 2026, before identifying four expired listings that readers should not treat as open unless DW Akademie announces an extension or relaunch.

DW Akademie opportunities and deadlines at a glance

Opportunity Main location or region Deadline Status on August 31, 2026
Podcast Storytelling and Production Trainers Western Balkans; online or offline August 31, 2026, 17:00 CET Open at the time of publication; urgent
Cultural Programme and Venue Partner for the Youth Meets Media Conference Phnom Penh, Cambodia September 4, 2026 Open
Digital Safety and AI Resilience Consultants Dar es Salaam, Tanzania September 7, 2026 Open
Ukrainian Youth for Media Literacy Stand-Up Comedy Berlin, Germany, with online rehearsals September 7, 2026 Open; extended deadline
Journalism and Media Trainers for SANA Syria; possible online mentoring September 15, 2026 Open
Journalism and Media Trainers for the Media Emergency Kit Syria; possible online mentoring September 15, 2026 Open

Applicants should verify the latest status on the relevant official page before submitting. A deadline shown without a time may close according to the organizer’s operating time zone, and DW Akademie may update, extend or withdraw a call.

About DW Akademie

DW Akademie is Deutsche Welle’s centre for international media development, journalism training and knowledge transfer. Its work supports freedom of expression, access to reliable information, constructive public dialogue and stronger media institutions. DW Akademie works with journalists, media organizations, civil society actors and other partners in developing and emerging economies, with support that includes funding from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, the German Federal Foreign Office and the European Union.

The opportunities below reflect that broad mandate. Some seek individual experts to deliver specialist training; others seek an organization able to host a programme; one invites young Ukrainians to take part in a media-literacy and stand-up comedy experience.

1. Podcast Storytelling and Production Trainers for Independent Media in the Western Balkans

The most urgent call is the DW Akademie opportunity for podcast trainers in the Western Balkans. DW Akademie intends to contract up to four experienced trainers to create and deliver a practical capacity-building programme for independent media organizations participating in SustainMedia II, a project concerned with the economic sustainability and innovation of independent media in the Western Balkans.

Purpose of the assignment

The programme is intended to strengthen both the editorial and technical abilities of journalists and media professionals. Participants should leave with the practical capacity to plan, produce, publish and improve audience-oriented podcasts that support public-interest journalism, expand audience reach and help independent outlets diversify their content.

The selected trainers will jointly develop a three-day programme that may be delivered online or offline. The official terms allow up to two preparation days, while implementation is expected between September and November 2026.

Expected training content

The assignment covers the full podcast workflow through three broad modules:

  1. Podcast storytelling and editorial development
    • Finding viable podcast concepts
    • Understanding audience needs
    • Editorial and content planning
    • Script development
    • Interviewing techniques
    • Narrative structure and storytelling
    • Selecting suitable podcast formats
    • Adapting content for different audiences
  2. Podcast production
    • Studio recording
    • Field recording
    • Mobile podcast production
    • Equipment selection
    • Sound quality
    • Editing workflows
    • Production planning
    • Publishing and distribution
    • Technical quality standards
  3. Audience development and practical production
    • Podcast branding
    • Audience engagement
    • Content promotion
    • Hands-on production exercises
    • Review of participant productions
    • Editorial feedback
    • Recommendations for sustainable podcast development

Trainer responsibilities

Selected trainers will be expected to collaborate on the training concept and agenda, combine theory with demonstrations and practical work, facilitate group and peer-learning activities, provide individual feedback, review participant assignments, monitor progress and coordinate closely with DW Akademie and the other trainers.

The required deliverables include a detailed concept and agenda, learning materials, practical exercises, delivery of the three-day programme, recommendations for participants’ continued development and a report on the training.

Experience DW Akademie is seeking

Strong applicants should be able to demonstrate:

  • Professional experience in journalism, storytelling and podcast production
  • Practical expertise in both studio and field production
  • Knowledge of podcast formats, editorial development and audience-focused content
  • Experience creating content for different audiences and digital platforms
  • A record of designing and delivering interactive workshops or training programmes
  • Strong facilitation, mentoring and coaching skills
  • Experience in media capacity-building
  • A sound understanding of the Western Balkans media environment
  • Excellent English

Knowledge of Albanian, Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian, Macedonian or Montenegrin is a strong advantage. Previous work with DW Akademie or a comparable international media-development organization is also advantageous.

How to apply

Applicants should send the following:

  • A letter of interest of no more than one page
  • A CV emphasizing podcast-production and training experience
  • Examples of relevant podcast productions and/or previous training work
  • A financial offer stating the proposed daily rate

Applications should be emailed to dw-akademie.western.balkans@dw.com with the subject line Application – Podcast Storytelling and Production Trainers – SustainMedia II.

Deadline: August 31, 2026, at 17:00 CET. This deadline was extended from August 21, 2026. Because it falls on the publication date of this article, interested applicants should act immediately and confirm that submissions are still being accepted. Full details appear in the official podcast trainers Terms of Reference.

2. Service Provider or Partner Organization for the Youth Meets Media Conference in Phnom Penh

DW Akademie is seeking a venue and partner organization in Phnom Penh to design and host an immersive cultural and discussion programme during the Youth Meets Media regional conference.

The conference, focused on media and information literacy and artificial intelligence in Central and Southeast Asia, will take place in Phnom Penh from October 23 to 25, 2026. It will bring together young people, media and information literacy stakeholders, and civil society representatives, chiefly from Cambodia, Myanmar, Mongolia, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.

Purpose of the programme

October 25 is reserved for a field-study experience that connects the conference’s main concerns with Cambodian society. The selected provider will host approximately 60 participants during the afternoon and evening and create a setting in which they can explore how disinformation, online safety, digital behaviour, exclusion and related issues affect communities, particularly young people and marginalized groups.

The programme should give meaningful visibility to Cambodia’s culture, history, society and present-day realities. It should also help participants compare Cambodian experiences with those in their own countries and regions.

Possible programme elements

DW Akademie welcomes creative proposals rather than prescribing one fixed format. A proposal may include:

  • A dedicated informal area for networking and intercultural exchange
  • Exhibitions, installations or media pieces related to the conference themes
  • Activities that introduce Cambodian culture, history and contemporary society
  • Dance, music or another cultural performance
  • Screenings of short films or documentaries
  • Discussions with filmmakers, protagonists, artists, speakers or experts
  • Interactive formats that explore youth and marginalized-community experiences

Relevant themes include artificial intelligence, disinformation, fact-checking, gender, inclusion, youth engagement, media and information literacy training, policy, online safety, scams, digital behaviour, content production and creative media formats.

What the provider must coordinate

The selected service provider should be capable of supplying or arranging:

  • Appropriate indoor and/or outdoor spaces for screenings, performances, exhibitions, activities and networking
  • Technical equipment such as a projector, screen and sound system
  • On-site technical support
  • Contributors such as performers, artists, filmmakers, speakers or experts
  • Catering and refreshments where appropriate
  • Overall logistical and programme coordination
  • A clear, itemized cost estimate

The target group is approximately 60 participants from Germany, Cambodia, Thailand, Myanmar, Bhutan, Mongolia, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.

Proposal requirements

Interested providers should submit:

  1. A brief programme concept explaining the proposed activities and contributors
  2. A description of the venue, available indoor and outdoor spaces, and maximum capacity
  3. An overview of the technical setup and available infrastructure
  4. A detailed cost estimate covering the venue, programme, equipment, catering, contributors and other relevant costs

Applications and questions should be sent to dw-akademie.digital-resilience@dw.com.

Deadline: September 4, 2026. The programme must be delivered in Phnom Penh on the afternoon and evening of October 25, 2026. Applicants should consult the official Phnom Penh partner Terms of Reference before preparing a proposal.

3. Digital Safety and AI Resilience Training Consultants in Tanzania

The Tanzania digital safety and AI resilience consultancy seeks two facilitators to jointly deliver a highly practical programme for community radio stations and media houses in Tanzania.

The assignment responds to the increasing exposure of media organizations to phishing, hacking, malware, ransomware, online harassment, surveillance, disinformation, unauthorized access and risks connected with artificial intelligence. It also recognizes that AI can support newsroom activities such as translation, transcription, production and audience engagement when organizations establish appropriate safeguards and governance.

Assignment schedule and payment structure

  • Location: Dar es Salaam, Tanzania; venue to be confirmed
  • Training dates: September 28 to October 2, 2026
  • Full-rate delivery: Five days
  • Preparation and reporting: Two days at half rate
  • Policy-development support: Two days at half rate
  • Working language: English
  • Reporting: Within three working days after the training

The financial proposal must account for a 15.83 percent withholding tax. Payment is subject to satisfactory completion and acceptance of the deliverables.

Main objectives

The two consultants will help participating media organizations to:

  • Improve organizational digital safety and cybersecurity
  • Identify and reduce risks affecting newsroom operations
  • Create practical safety policies, incident-response procedures and continuity plans
  • Protect journalists, community correspondents, confidential sources and organizational information
  • Prepare for the responsible adoption and governance of AI tools
  • Continue serving women, young people and rural communities in a safer digital environment

Training areas

The programme must be learner-centred, participatory and strongly practical, with at least half of the training devoted to exercises and hands-on learning. Topics include:

  • Organizational threat mapping, information-asset identification and vulnerability assessment
  • Device security, digital hygiene, malware, ransomware and endpoint protection
  • Password management and multi-factor authentication
  • Secure storage, data-retention and data-destruction practices
  • Confidential-source and whistleblower protection
  • Metadata and digital footprints
  • Encrypted communications, secure email, and identity verification
  • Phishing and social-engineering simulations
  • Incident reporting and cyber-crisis management
  • Backup strategies, disaster recovery and continuity of operations
  • AI opportunities in journalism
  • Misinformation, deepfakes and other AI-related risks
  • AI governance and newsroom policies
  • Online violence against women journalists
  • Risks affecting young reporters and community correspondents
  • Protection of vulnerable contributors and sources
  • AI bias and the representation of women and youth

Expected outputs

By the end of the programme, participants and their organizations should have stronger knowledge and practical skills, completed digital-risk assessments, draft Digital Safety Action Plans, draft Cyber Incident Response Plans and draft AI Use and Governance Guidelines.

The consultants must provide a finalized agenda, session plans, materials, practical tools, assessment results, documentation of participant outputs and a detailed post-training report with observations and recommendations.

Required expertise

Applicants should demonstrate experience in digital safety, cybersecurity, organizational resilience, responsible AI, AI governance, newsroom operations and media development. They should also have worked with media organizations, journalists, civil society organizations or human-rights actors and be able to use adult-learning and participatory approaches. Gender-sensitive facilitation, sound training design and strong time management are required. Experience in East Africa is an advantage.

Two individuals may apply together, or a consulting team or institution may propose two qualified facilitators. The facilitators may be based in Tanzania or another country, provided they understand the East African media context.

Application documents

Applicants must submit:

  1. A letter expressing interest
  2. Updated CVs
  3. An organizational profile, where applicable
  4. A technical proposal of no more than three pages explaining the methodology, approach and training design
  5. Evidence of at least three similar assignments
  6. A financial proposal showing the daily rate and total cost, including the 15.83 percent withholding tax

Send the application to akademie.uganda@dw.com, copying warda.mansour@dw.com and moses.mutente@dw.com.

Deadline: September 7, 2026. The full requirements are available in the official Tanzania consultancy Terms of Reference.

4. Ukrainian Youth Media Literacy and Stand-Up Comedy Programme in Berlin

The DW Akademie media literacy stand-up comedy programme offers Ukrainian young people aged 12 to 16 who live in Berlin an unusual opportunity to combine comedy, public performance and critical engagement with digital information.

Rather than teaching media literacy only through conventional lessons, the programme helps participants transform their observations about fake news, memes, TikTok trends, algorithms and information overload into original stand-up monologues.

What participants will learn

The programme is designed to help young participants:

  • Write jokes and social monologues with a clear message
  • Explain how online information environments work in an engaging way
  • Develop improvisation and comedy skills
  • Improve voice control, breathing and diction
  • Understand joke structure, storytelling and speech structure
  • Connect with an audience and manage performance stress
  • Recognize fake news, manipulation, online trends and algorithmic influence
  • Analyze examples from the Ukrainian information environment
  • Protect personal data and adopt safer online behaviour
  • Develop an individual script and organize a complete stage performance

Format and important dates

Preparation includes online rehearsals, individual script development and guidance on structuring each performance.

  • In-person rehearsal in Berlin: October 11, 2026
  • Stand-up show in Berlin: October 12, 2026

At the final show, participants will present their own stand-up monologues.

The guidance team brings experience in stand-up comedy, radio, public broadcasting, documentary and digital production, stage speech, youth engagement, meme analysis, media literacy, cyberbullying education, journalism, TikTok content and audiovisual teaching. This range of expertise is intended to help participants improve both the substance of their media-literacy messages and the confidence with which they perform them.

Deadline: September 7, 2026. The deadline was extended. Eligible young people should complete the official online registration form and review the English programme information.

5. Journalism and Media Trainers for the Syrian Arab News Agency

Under the European Union-funded Fill the Space project, implemented by DW Akademie with Fatabyyano, DW Akademie is forming a pool of trainers for the Syrian Arab News Agency.

The trainers will support the professional and institutional development of SANA staff and correspondents. Assignments are expected to take place intermittently from October 2026 through April 2027; inclusion in the pool does not create continuous employment or guarantee a contract.

Potential training themes

Applicants may indicate one or more areas that match their expertise:

  1. Editorial standards and journalism ethics
  2. News writing and editing
  3. Television journalism and media appearance
  4. Visual storytelling and multimedia production
  5. Mobile journalism
  6. Photography and photojournalism
  7. Video production and editing
  8. Digital journalism and social media management
  9. Verification and fact-checking
  10. Public-service journalism
  11. Conflict-sensitive and transitional-justice reporting
  12. Digital security and safety for journalists
  13. Audience engagement and community-centred journalism
  14. Responsible use of artificial intelligence in journalism
  15. Other relevant journalism and media subjects identified during implementation

Scope of work

Selected trainers will review background material, adapt content to assessed needs, prepare agendas and learning resources, lead interactive and practice-oriented sessions, facilitate simulations and assignments, assess learning, coach participants, coordinate with DW Akademie and SANA, and submit the agreed materials and final report.

Training may take place in Damascus and other locations in Syria, with possible online mentoring and follow-up sessions. Exact preparation days, training days, mentoring work and schedules will be agreed for each assignment.

Eligibility and preferred assets

Applicants must be native Arabic speakers, have at least two years of media experience and preferably media-training experience in the Western Asia and North Africa region, demonstrate commitment to independent and ethical journalism, and not be subject to European Union sanctions or blacklisting.

A journalism, media or related degree is an asset. Previous DW Akademie training or training-of-trainers experience is a strong asset, while previous experience with the Syrian context is also valued. DW Akademie particularly encourages applications from Syrian local, community, regional, exile and independent journalists with strong community ties.

Deliverables and financial arrangements

Expected outputs may include:

  • A detailed agenda and methodology
  • Presentations, exercises and case studies
  • Participant handouts
  • Pre- and post-training assessments where requested
  • Participant evaluations and attendance records
  • A final narrative report with recommendations
  • Electronic copies of all training materials

Deliverables should be submitted in English unless otherwise agreed. Trainers will be contracted individually, fees will be agreed according to the approved budget and procurement rules, applicable travel and accommodation will follow DW Akademie policy, and payment will be made after satisfactory completion and acceptance.

How to apply

Submit one merged PDF in English containing:

  • An updated CV
  • A motivation letter naming the desired theme or themes and summarizing relevant training experience
  • The expected daily training fee and preparation-day fee in euros
  • Contact details for two professional references
  • The applicant’s full name and address
  • Confirmation of whether the applicant has a bank account outside Syria

Email the file to dw-akademie.fillthespace@dw.com with the subject Application – SANA Trainer – [Applicant Name]. Incomplete applications will not be considered, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Deadline: September 15, 2026. Applicants should rely on the contact details and instructions in the official SANA trainer Terms of Reference.

6. Journalism and Media Trainers for the Media Emergency Kit Programme in Syria

DW Akademie is also forming a separate pool of trainers and co-trainers for a Media Emergency Kit programme under the Fill the Space project.

This opportunity focuses on strengthening the capacities of Syrian independent journalists and media outlets. Successful applicants will first participate in a specialized four-day online Training of Trainers for the Media Emergency Kit and may then receive assignment-based training work between October 2026 and April 2027.

Training themes

Assignments may cover one or more of the following:

  • Journalism ethics
  • Fact-checking and verification
  • Professional local journalism beyond breaking news
  • Conflict-sensitive reporting and transitional justice
  • Audience outreach and community management
  • Four-dimensional safety: physical, psychological, legal and digital
  • Efficient and ethical use of artificial intelligence in media work

Responsibilities

The trainers will review assigned topics and project materials, adapt course content, create agendas and learning resources, lead participatory sessions, facilitate exercises and simulations, assess learning, coach participants, coordinate with DW Akademie and submit training materials and a final report.

Training may be delivered in Damascus and other parts of Syria and may include online mentoring and follow-up. The number of training days, preparation days and mentoring assignments will be agreed case by case.

Eligibility and application package

The core eligibility requirements are the same as those for the SANA trainer pool: native Arabic, at least two years of media experience and preferably training experience in the Western Asia and North Africa region, commitment to independent and ethical journalism, and no European Union sanctions or blacklisting. A relevant degree, DW Akademie training-of-trainers experience and familiarity with Syria are assets. Syrian local, community, regional, exile and independent journalists are particularly encouraged.

Applicants should send one English-language merged PDF containing an updated CV, a motivation letter naming the relevant theme or themes, the expected training-day and preparation-day fees in euros, two professional references, full name and address, and confirmation of whether they have a bank account outside Syria.

Send applications to dw-akademie.fillthespace@dw.com with the subject Application – MEK Trainer – [Applicant Name].

Deadline: September 15, 2026. Selection for the pool is not a guarantee of a future contract; assignments depend on project needs, expertise and availability. Review the official Media Emergency Kit trainer Terms of Reference before applying.

Recently expired DW Akademie listings still shown on the official page

The following opportunities appeared on the official hub on August 31, 2026, but their stated deadlines had passed. They are included here to prevent confusion and to help readers identify the type of work DW Akademie may advertise again.

Tunis-based Project Manager for North and West Africa

The Tunis-based project manager opportunity sought an experienced professional to manage donor-funded media-development work across North and West Africa. The proposed contract period was September 15, 2026, to August 31, 2028. The role covered a women’s empowerment and socioeconomic-inclusion project in Morocco and work concerning the effects of migration in Morocco, Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire and Guinea.

Deadline: August 28, 2026. This listing had expired by August 31, 2026.

Evaluation of DW Akademie Projects in Africa

The Africa project evaluation call invited evaluators for projects supported by Germany’s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development. The projects run from January 2025 to December 2027, with evaluations expected during their final year. The regional groupings included Ghana; Kenya; Namibia and Southern Africa; Uganda and Tanzania; and a Sahel-plus grouping covering Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, Mali, Niger and Senegal.

Deadline: August 30, 2026. This listing had expired by August 31, 2026.

Mobile Journalism Trainers in Montenegro

The mobile journalism trainer call in Montenegro sought two trainers for a Young Media Makers Fellowship workshop in Petrovac from October 12 to 14, 2026, followed by an online session. The work focused on mobile content production, digital storytelling and practical skills for young media professionals in the Western Balkans, alongside the Media Innovation Forum.

Deadline: August 27, 2026. This listing had expired by August 31, 2026.

Research and Monitoring on Disinformation and Hate Speech in Syria

The Syria disinformation and hate-speech research call sought an organization or expert team to research and monitor campaigns targeting Syrian media actors, journalists and fact-checkers, with attention to narratives influencing Syrian audiences aged 18 to 45.

The anticipated work included baseline analysis of narratives, actors and platforms, quantitative and qualitative monitoring, periodic reports in Arabic and English, briefings for newsrooms and civil society organizations, and a final synthesis.

Deadline: August 27, 2026. This listing had expired by August 31, 2026.

Applicants interested in any expired listing should not send a late application unless the relevant official page is updated with an extension or DW Akademie confirms that submissions are still accepted.

Practical application checklist

Before applying for any current DW Akademie opportunity, candidates and organizations should:

  1. Open the individual opportunity page rather than relying only on the central hub.
  2. Download and read the complete Terms of Reference.
  3. Confirm the exact deadline, time zone, subject line and submission email.
  4. Tailor the CV, interest letter or proposal to the stated thematic area and deliverables.
  5. Include every requested financial detail, tax component and supporting document.
  6. Respect page limits and file-format instructions, including merged-PDF requirements.
  7. Demonstrate relevant regional or contextual knowledge with specific examples.
  8. Provide evidence of previous assignments, productions or training work where requested.
  9. Check that references, cost estimates, contact information and attachments are complete.
  10. Submit early enough to resolve email, upload or time-zone problems before the deadline.

Frequently asked questions

Are all listings on the DW Akademie opportunities page still open?

No. The official hub can display opportunities with recently passed deadlines. Applicants must read the date on each individual page and its downloadable Terms of Reference. As of August 31, 2026, six calls were still actionable, including the Western Balkans podcast trainer deadline later that same day.

Can applicants based outside the advertised country apply?

It depends on the call. The Tanzania Terms of Reference explicitly permit facilitators based in Tanzania or elsewhere, provided they have the necessary expertise and understand the East African media context. Other calls may require local delivery capacity, regional knowledge, language skills or residence in a specific city. Applicants should follow the exact wording of the relevant terms.

Does joining a trainer pool guarantee paid work?

No. The SANA and Media Emergency Kit calls state that admission to a qualified-trainer pool does not guarantee a contract. Assignments will depend on project needs, trainer expertise and availability.

Are financial offers required?

Most professional calls request some form of financial information. This may be a daily rate, preparation-day rate, total cost, or detailed programme budget. The Tanzania call specifically requires the applicant to include the stated withholding tax in the rate.

Where should applicants obtain the final application instructions?

The controlling source should be the individual official opportunity page and its linked Terms of Reference. Applicants should copy email addresses and subject lines carefully from the downloadable document and check the page again immediately before submission.

Conclusion

The 2026 DW Akademie opportunities and tenders currently provide several distinct routes into international media-development work. Experienced podcast producers can support independent media in the Western Balkans; digital-security and responsible-AI specialists can work with Tanzanian media houses; Arabic-speaking journalists and trainers can join Syria-focused trainer pools; a Phnom Penh organization can design a culturally grounded programme for a regional conference; and Ukrainian young people in Berlin can develop media literacy through stand-up comedy.

The deadlines are close, beginning with the podcast trainer call on August 31, 2026, at 17:00 CET, followed by the Phnom Penh partnership on September 4, the Tanzania consultancy and Ukrainian youth programme on September 7, and the two Syria trainer pools on September 15. Applicants should prioritize the most urgent opportunity, use the exact official instructions and submit a complete, tailored application before the relevant closing time.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the WWF-Amano Fellowship 2027, an intensive nine-month virtual leadership development programme designed to support young Ugandans who are actively contributing to conservation, climate action, environmental education, sustainable development, or community transformation.

Organised by WWF International in collaboration with the Amano So Global Mentorship Network, the fellowship provides emerging environmental leaders with access to mentorship, expert-led workshops, peer learning, strategic leadership development and an international network of young changemakers.

The programme is particularly suitable for young people who are already taking action in their communities and want to strengthen their ability to create meaningful and lasting impact for nature, people and sustainable development.

About the WWF-Amano Fellowship 2027

The WWF-Amano Fellowship is a nine-month virtual leadership development programme created to help emerging conservation and environmental leaders develop the knowledge, confidence, networks and practical leadership skills required to advance positive change.

The fellowship combines several areas of development, including:

  • Conservation awareness
  • Leadership development
  • Strategic thinking
  • Emotional resilience
  • Mentorship
  • Peer learning
  • Community engagement
  • Environmental advocacy

One of the major advantages of the programme is its virtual format. Fellows can participate in the programme while continuing their existing employment, education, businesses, conservation activities or community initiatives.

Rather than requiring participants to leave their ongoing work, the fellowship is designed to complement what they are already doing.

What Is the Aim of the WWF-Amano Fellowship?

The programme is focused on developing a new generation of environmental leaders who can contribute to biodiversity conservation and sustainable development at the community level.

Many environmental challenges require strong leadership beyond technical knowledge. Young people working in conservation and community development may need to understand how to build partnerships, influence decision-makers, communicate effectively, develop strategies and maintain resilience when working on complex environmental issues.

The WWF-Amano Fellowship seeks to strengthen these abilities by bringing together young changemakers for a structured learning and mentorship experience.

Through the programme, fellows can develop the capacity to:

  • Strengthen their leadership abilities.
  • Improve their strategic thinking.
  • Build professional and personal networks.
  • Learn from experienced conservation professionals.
  • Exchange ideas with other young environmental leaders.
  • Better understand conservation and sustainable development challenges.
  • Increase their ability to influence environmental initiatives and policies.
  • Develop approaches for creating measurable community impact.

Fellowship Duration and Format

The WWF-Amano Fellowship will run for nine months.

The programme will be conducted online, allowing participants to remain active in their existing professional, academic or community activities.

The virtual programme is expected to involve activities such as:

  • Mentorship meetings
  • Group mentoring sessions
  • One-on-one coaching
  • Expert-led workshops
  • Guest speaker sessions
  • Peer discussions
  • Knowledge-sharing activities
  • Other online learning and leadership development activities

Participants will therefore need access to a reliable internet connection and sufficient time to participate consistently.

Key Benefits of the WWF-Amano Fellowship

Selected fellows will have access to several leadership and professional development opportunities.

1. Group Mentoring

Participants will take part in group mentoring with experienced conservation professionals. These sessions provide opportunities to learn from individuals with practical experience in environmental and conservation work.

2. Personalised One-on-One Coaching

The programme also provides personalised coaching, allowing fellows to receive more focused guidance as they develop their leadership capabilities.

3. Expert-Led Workshops

Fellows will participate in interactive workshops led by experienced environmental leaders and professionals.

These sessions are intended to strengthen practical knowledge and expose participants to different approaches to conservation, leadership and sustainable development.

4. International and Regional Networking

The fellowship brings together young changemakers from Uganda, Africa and beyond.

This provides an opportunity to establish relationships with other people working on environmental and community issues and potentially develop future collaborations.

5. Peer Learning

Participants will have opportunities to share experiences, challenges and solutions with fellow environmental leaders.

Peer learning can be particularly valuable because participants may be working on different environmental challenges and can learn from approaches being used in other communities.

6. Leadership Development

The programme focuses strongly on developing leadership capabilities, including strategic thinking, confidence, resilience and the ability to influence positive change.

7. Greater Conservation Knowledge

Fellows can strengthen their understanding of conservation and sustainable development issues and explore approaches that can be applied within their own communities.

8. Stronger Professional Networks

Participants can build social and professional capital that may help them engage more effectively with conservation initiatives, community organisations and environmental policy processes.

9. Practical Community Impact

The fellowship is designed for people who are already involved in creating positive change. The knowledge, mentorship and networks gained through the programme can therefore be applied to existing or future community and environmental initiatives.

Who Is the WWF-Amano Fellowship Looking For?

The programme is intended for young Ugandan environmental and community leaders aged 21–30.

Applicants should be people who are already demonstrating a commitment to environmental or community-based action rather than individuals with no previous involvement in these areas.

The programme particularly welcomes applicants who are contributing to areas such as:

  • Nature conservation
  • Biodiversity protection
  • Climate advocacy
  • Environmental education
  • Sustainable entrepreneurship
  • Community development
  • Environmental awareness
  • Conservation-related initiatives
  • Other activities contributing to positive environmental or community change

Eligibility Requirements

To be considered for the WWF-Amano Fellowship, applicants should meet the following requirements.

Age

Applicants must be 21 to 30 years old.

Nationality

The fellowship is specifically open to young Ugandans.

Demonstrated Environmental or Community Engagement

Applicants should have evidence that they have been involved in conservation, environmental activities, climate advocacy, environmental education, sustainable entrepreneurship or related community initiatives.

The fellowship is therefore aimed at emerging leaders who are already doing work that contributes to positive change.

Evidence of Impact

Applicants are expected to demonstrate how their work, project or initiative has contributed to positive environmental or community outcomes.

This could include involvement in projects, advocacy activities, education initiatives, conservation programmes, community mobilisation or other relevant work.

English Language

Applicants must have strong spoken and written English skills because programme activities will be conducted in English.

Time Commitment

Fellows must be able to dedicate approximately 5–8 hours per month to fellowship activities.

This may include:

  • Mentor group meetings
  • Expert workshops
  • Guest speaker sessions
  • Peer discussions
  • Other fellowship activities

Internet Access

Because the fellowship is delivered virtually, applicants should have reliable internet connectivity that allows them to participate in online meetings, workshops and other programme activities.

Who Is Particularly Encouraged to Apply?

The programme highlights the importance of supporting diverse and emerging environmental leaders.

In particular, the fellowship encourages applications from:

  • Individuals from local communities involved in conservation.
  • Individuals from Indigenous communities with demonstrated conservation involvement.
  • Young women working in environmental and conservation fields.
  • Applicants from underserved or marginalised communities.
  • Early-career emerging environmental leaders.
  • Mid-career emerging leaders who meet the age and other requirements.

The key consideration is that applicants should be able to demonstrate genuine involvement and positive impact in conservation, environmental action or community development.

What Kind of Experience Can Strengthen an Application?

Applicants should be able to demonstrate practical involvement in environmental or community activities.

Relevant experience may include participation in:

  • Conservation projects
  • Climate action campaigns
  • Environmental education programmes
  • Community environmental initiatives
  • Sustainable businesses or entrepreneurship
  • Biodiversity-related activities
  • Community awareness campaigns
  • Environmental advocacy
  • Youth-led environmental initiatives
  • Projects addressing local environmental challenges

Applicants should focus on demonstrating what they have done, the role they played and the impact their work created.

How to Apply for the WWF-Amano Fellowship 2027

Interested applicants are required to prepare a one-page brief about themselves.

The brief should highlight the applicant’s:

  • Background
  • Leadership experience
  • Conservation involvement
  • Environmental activities
  • Community engagement
  • Relevant achievements or impact

The application should clearly provide the following information:

  1. Full name
  2. Date of birth
  3. Email address
  4. Telephone number
  5. Evidence of conservation, environmental or community engagement experience

Applicants should ensure that their information is clear, accurate and easy to review.

Where to Submit the Application

Applications should be submitted by email to:

recruitment@wwfuganda.org

Applicants should ensure that their application reaches the organisation before the stated deadline.

WWF-Amano Fellowship 2027 Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

16 September 2026

Applicants are encouraged to prepare and submit their applications early rather than waiting until the final day.

Since the application requires evidence of previous conservation, environmental or community engagement, applicants should allow enough time to prepare a clear one-page profile and supporting information.

Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable for Young Environmental Leaders

Environmental leadership requires more than simply understanding environmental problems. Young leaders often need the ability to mobilise communities, communicate ideas, build partnerships, influence policies and develop practical solutions.

The WWF-Amano Fellowship combines leadership development with conservation awareness, mentorship and networking.

For a young Ugandan already working on environmental or community issues, the programme could therefore provide an opportunity to strengthen existing capabilities while remaining engaged in ongoing activities.

The emphasis on strategic thinking, emotional resilience and peer learning can also help participants approach complex environmental challenges with greater confidence and a broader perspective.

Learn more about this opportunity HERE

Application Preparation Tips

Before submitting an application, prospective applicants should consider the following:

Clearly explain your impact

Do not simply list environmental activities you have participated in. Explain what you actually contributed and what changed as a result.

Highlight leadership

The fellowship is a leadership development programme, so applicants should demonstrate examples of taking initiative, leading activities, mobilising people or helping to solve community problems.

Keep the one-page profile focused

Because the application requires a one-page brief, applicants should prioritise their strongest and most relevant experiences rather than attempting to include every activity they have ever undertaken.

Demonstrate your environmental commitment

Make the connection between your experience and conservation, climate action, environmental education, sustainable entrepreneurship or community development clear.

Check your contact information

Ensure that your full name, email address and telephone number are correct so that the organisers can contact you if necessary.

Apply before the deadline

Applications must be submitted by 16 September 2026. Early submission is recommended.

Conclusion

The WWF-Amano Fellowship 2027 provides an important leadership development opportunity for young Ugandans already working to create positive environmental and community change.

Through its nine-month virtual format, the programme combines conservation awareness with leadership development, strategic thinking, emotional resilience, mentorship, expert workshops and peer learning. Fellows can remain active in their studies, employment, businesses or community initiatives while developing new skills and expanding their professional networks.

The fellowship is particularly relevant to young conservationists, climate advocates, environmental educators, sustainable entrepreneurs and community changemakers who can demonstrate genuine involvement and positive impact.

Eligible applicants should prepare their one-page profile carefully and submit their application to recruitment@wwfuganda.org before the 16 September 2026 deadline.

This opportunity is specifically for young Ugandan environmental and community leaders aged 21–30, making it a strong platform for emerging leaders who want to strengthen their ability to contribute to conservation, sustainable development and lasting community transformation.

Discover more global Fellowship opportunities on OFY HERE
