item.content:encoded:
Wallace Fellowship 2027–2028 at Harvard’s I Tatti: $5,200 Monthly Stipend for Scholars Researching the Italian Renaissance

The Wallace Fellowship at Harvard University’s Villa I Tatti – The Harvard University Center for Italian Renaissance Studies offers scholars an opportunity to dedicate several months to advanced research on the historiography, influence, transformation, and continuing impact of the Italian Renaissance in the modern era.

Supported by a generous grant from The Lila Wallace – Reader’s Digest Fund, the Wallace Fellowship is designed for scholars whose research explores how the Italian Renaissance has been understood, interpreted, transformed, and represented from the 19th century through the 21st century.

The fellowship provides selected scholars with a residential research period in Florence, Italy, allowing them to concentrate on their proposed projects while benefiting from access to Harvard’s scholarly resources and the intellectual community at I Tatti.

Up to four Wallace Fellowships are awarded each year, and the residential fellowship can last either four or six months.

Applications for the fellowship must be submitted by November 16, 2026, while letters of recommendation must be submitted by November 21, 2026.

About the Wallace Fellowship

The Wallace Fellowship is intended for scholars conducting research into the Italian Renaissance and its relationship with the modern era.

The fellowship recognizes that the Renaissance continues to have a significant influence on modern scholarship, culture, artistic production, architecture, literature, music, philosophy, political thought, museums, collecting practices, and other areas of intellectual and cultural life.

Rather than limiting applicants to one specific academic discipline, the fellowship welcomes a broad range of research projects that examine the ways the Renaissance has survived, been interpreted, transformed, or commented upon during the 19th, 20th, and 21st centuries.

This makes the fellowship potentially relevant to researchers working across multiple fields, provided that their proposed project has a meaningful connection to the historiography or impact of the Italian Renaissance in the modern era.

Research Areas Covered by the Wallace Fellowship

Applicants can propose projects addressing a wide range of topics connected to the Renaissance and modernity.

Potential areas of research include:

  • Historiography of the Italian Renaissance
  • The impact of the Renaissance on modern thought and culture
  • Modern interpretations of the Italian Renaissance
  • Reactions to Renaissance ideas and traditions
  • Transformations of Renaissance concepts in the modern era
  • Commentary on the Renaissance and its relationship with modernity
  • Museum history
  • Collecting history
  • Renaissance influences on modern art
  • Renaissance influences on modern architecture
  • Photography
  • Landscape architecture
  • Literature
  • Music
  • Philosophy
  • Political thought
  • History
  • Material culture
  • Religion
  • Science

The fellowship therefore provides considerable intellectual scope for researchers whose work connects Renaissance studies with developments and debates in the modern period.

Apply HERE

A Residential Research Opportunity in Florence

One of the defining features of the Wallace Fellowship is its residential nature.

Fellows are expected to live in the Florence area during their fellowship and spend at least three days per week at I Tatti.

This arrangement is intended to give scholars the time and environment necessary to concentrate deeply on their research.

I Tatti describes the fellowship environment as providing Fellows with valuable time to pursue their studies with a minimum of obligations and interruptions, while also giving them access to substantial scholarly resources.

The combination of dedicated research time and access to an active academic community makes the fellowship particularly suitable for scholars who need an extended period of concentrated research.

Learn more HERE

Life and Academic Community at I Tatti

Wallace Fellows are not isolated researchers. They become part of the broader scholarly environment at I Tatti.

Each year, certain activities organized at the center are reserved for Fellows, and Fellows are expected to participate in the wider intellectual community.

This includes joining:

  • Conferences
  • Lectures
  • Concerts
  • Other scholarly and cultural activities organized at the center

The expectation of collegial participation means that applicants are evaluated not only on the quality of their research but also on their potential contribution to the intellectual life of the Harvard Center.

Wallace Fellowship Duration

The Wallace Fellowship is a residential fellowship lasting either:

  • Four months, or
  • Six months

Applicants are asked to indicate their preferred fellowship period when applying.

They must choose between:

  • Fall: September through December
  • Winter-Spring: January through June

Applicants should therefore consider their research schedule carefully before selecting their preferred term.

Wallace Fellowship Financial Support

Selected Fellows receive significant financial support during their residence in Florence.

The fellowship provides:

Monthly Grant

Fellows receive:

USD 5,200 per month

This monthly grant is intended to support the Fellow during the residential research period.

Relocation Supplement

In addition to the monthly grant, Fellows may receive a one-time relocation supplement of up to USD 1,800.

This additional support is intended to help offset relocation expenses associated with moving to Florence for the fellowship.

Housing Support in Florence

Because the Wallace Fellowship is residential, housing is an important part of the fellowship arrangement.

When possible, an apartment will be set aside for the Fellow’s use rent-free, although the Fellow will be responsible for utility charges.

If an apartment is not available, a housing subsidy will be provided to help offset rental costs.

This arrangement can substantially reduce the financial burden associated with living in Florence during the fellowship.

However, applicants should understand that housing is subject to availability and that Fellows may need to use the housing subsidy if an apartment cannot be provided.

Access to Harvard’s Resources

Wallace Fellows enjoy the privileges available to Fellows at the Harvard Center.

One particularly important resource is the Biblioteca Berenson, which Fellows can use seven days a week.

Fellows also have the opportunity to participate in lunch with other appointees from Monday through Friday.

Although Term Fellows do not receive a private office or study, they are provided with their own desk or carrel in the Library.

This arrangement is designed to provide scholars with a dedicated workspace while keeping them connected to the research environment of the center.

Important Restrictions During the Fellowship

Applicants should carefully consider the fellowship’s requirements before applying.

Wallace Fellows are expected to devote themselves to the research project for which they were selected.

During the fellowship:

  • Fellows must work solely on the project with which they applied.
  • They may not simultaneously work on editing other books or article projects.
  • They may not take on other obligations such as teaching positions, including part-time teaching.
  • The fellowship cannot be held concurrently with another fellowship or award.
  • The fellowship cannot be deferred.
  • Term Fellowships can be held only once.

These conditions emphasize that the fellowship is intended to provide scholars with dedicated time for one substantial research project.

Who Can Apply for the Wallace Fellowship?

Applicants must meet several academic and professional requirements.

At the time of application, scholars must already have a PhD.

Applicants will be required to upload a scan of their PhD certificate as part of the application process.

Applicants also:

  • Must not be working toward a second PhD at the time of application.
  • Must be prepared to work solely on their proposed fellowship project.
  • Must be conversant in English.
  • Must have familiarity with Italian.
  • Should have a research project that falls within the fellowship’s thematic scope.
  • Must be able to conduct most of their research in Florence.

The fellowship gives priority to early- and mid-career scholars.

Applicants From All Nations Are Welcome

The Wallace Fellowship is open to scholars from all nations.

The program does not restrict applications to scholars from a particular country or continent.

Importantly, I Tatti gives special consideration to candidates who do not have regular access to research materials and facilities in Italy.

This means that scholars who face limited access to Italian research resources may receive particular consideration during the selection process.

Academic Fields Eligible for Consideration

The fellowship has a broad interdisciplinary focus.

Proposed projects may address the Renaissance’s historiography or impact in fields including:

  • Art
  • Architecture
  • Landscape architecture
  • History
  • Literature
  • Material culture
  • Music
  • Philosophy
  • Religion
  • Science

Applicants should therefore focus on demonstrating a strong intellectual connection between their proposed research and the Italian Renaissance’s role, interpretation, influence, or transformation in the modern era.

How Applications Are Evaluated

Applications are evaluated by international scholars.

The selection process considers several elements of an applicant’s academic profile and proposed research.

Particular attention is given to:

  1. The strength of the proposed project

The research proposal should present a strong and compelling scholarly project.

  1. Potential for original results

Applicants should demonstrate that their research has the potential to produce original findings or meaningful scholarly contributions.

  1. Curriculum vitae

The applicant’s academic and research background is an important component of the evaluation.

  1. Contribution to the intellectual community

The selection committee also considers the candidate’s ability to contribute collegially to the intellectual life of the Harvard Center.

Applicants should therefore think beyond simply presenting a strong research topic. They should also demonstrate that they can participate constructively in the scholarly community at I Tatti.

Previous Appointments at I Tatti

The Wallace Fellowship is intended primarily for scholars who have not previously held appointments at I Tatti.

Term Fellowships can only be held once.

However, there is an exception for Graduate Fellows.

Applicants who have previously held an appointment at I Tatti should therefore carefully review the eligibility conditions before preparing an application.

Visa, Residence Permit, and Health Coverage

International scholars selected for the fellowship are responsible for arranging the documentation and coverage required for their residence in Italy.

The Fellow is responsible for obtaining:

  • A visa, where required
  • A permesso di soggiorno (residence permit)
  • Health coverage
  • Appropriate documentation and arrangements for accompanying family members, where applicable

Applicants should determine whether they require a visa and, if necessary, obtain it before traveling to Italy.

These immigration and health-related responsibilities should be considered when planning for the fellowship.

Outside Funding and Salary

Applicants who receive a partial salary or outside grants must disclose this information.

Such funding should be indicated either:

  • In the application, or
  • In subsequent correspondence with the Director

Permission must be received if the applicant has partial salary or outside grant support.

Applicants should therefore provide accurate information about any other sources of financial support connected to their research or professional circumstances.

Application Language

Applications for the Wallace Fellowship may be written in either:

  • English, or
  • Italian

This gives eligible scholars flexibility in presenting their research proposal and other application materials.

However, applicants are expected to be conversant in English and have familiarity with Italian.

Wallace Fellowship Application Deadline

The main application deadline is:

November 16, 2026

Applications must be submitted electronically by midnight, Cambridge, Massachusetts time, on November 16, 2026.

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their materials because technical or administrative problems could potentially interfere with a timely submission.

Recommendation Letter Deadline

Letters of recommendation have a separate deadline:

November 21, 2026

Applicants must have two scholars who know their work well submit recommendations online by this date.

The recommendation letters may be written in:

  • English, or
  • Italian

Applicants are strongly encouraged to register their referees as early as possible through the reference tab so that the referees have sufficient time to complete and submit their recommendations.

Choosing Recommendation Writers

Applicants should select two scholars who know their academic and research work well.

A strong recommendation can help provide the selection committee with additional insight into:

  • The applicant’s academic ability
  • Research experience
  • Scholarly potential
  • Quality of previous work
  • Capacity to undertake the proposed project

Applicants should also make sure that their referees understand the nature of the proposed project and the relevant submission deadline.

The applicant is responsible for informing the scholars writing on their behalf about the project and recommendation deadline.

One Fellowship Type Per Academic Year

Scholars can apply for only one type of fellowship at I Tatti per academic year.

Applicants should therefore carefully consider which I Tatti fellowship best corresponds to their research profile before submitting an application.

Submitting applications for multiple fellowship types during the same academic year is not permitted.

How to Prepare a Strong Wallace Fellowship Application

Because the selection committee pays particular attention to the proposed project, applicants should make the research proposal one of the strongest parts of their application.

A well-prepared application should clearly communicate:

1. The central research question

Explain exactly what the project seeks to investigate.

2. The connection to the Italian Renaissance

Clearly establish how the proposed research relates to the historiography, influence, transformation, survival, or interpretation of the Italian Renaissance in the modern era.

3. The modern-era dimension

The Wallace Fellowship focuses specifically on the relationship between the Renaissance and the modern era. Applicants should make this connection clear.

4. The potential for original results

Explain what new contribution the research could make and why the project has the potential to produce original findings.

5. Why Florence is important

Since applicants must be able to carry out most of their research in Florence, it is useful for the proposal to demonstrate why access to resources in Florence and at I Tatti is important for the project.

6. A clear research plan

Applicants should have a realistic understanding of what they intend to accomplish during their four- or six-month residential period.

Why the Wallace Fellowship Is a Significant Research Opportunity

The Wallace Fellowship combines several elements that can be valuable for scholars undertaking advanced research.

The fellowship provides:

  • A dedicated residential research period in Florence
  • USD 5,200 per month
  • Up to USD 1,800 in relocation support
  • Potential rent-free apartment accommodation when available
  • Housing subsidy when an apartment is unavailable
  • Access to the Biblioteca Berenson seven days a week
  • A dedicated desk or carrel in the Library
  • Participation in the intellectual community at I Tatti
  • Access to conferences, lectures, concerts, and other activities
  • The opportunity to work alongside scholars and other appointees
  • A research environment designed to minimize competing obligations

For scholars whose work requires substantial engagement with Italian Renaissance materials and resources in Florence, these features can provide a valuable environment for concentrated academic research.

Key Facts About the Wallace Fellowship

Detail Information
Fellowship Wallace Fellowship
Host institution Harvard University’s I Tatti
Location Florence, Italy
Duration Four or six months
Fellowships awarded Up to four per year
Monthly grant USD 5,200
Relocation supplement Up to USD 1,800
Housing Apartment when available or housing subsidy
Main application language English or Italian
PhD requirement PhD must be held at application
English requirement Applicants must be conversant in English
Italian requirement Familiarity with Italian required
Geographic eligibility Scholars from all nations
Main deadline November 16, 2026
Recommendation deadline November 21, 2026

Important Dates to Remember

Applicants should keep the following dates in their calendars:

November 16, 2026: Main application deadline. Applications must be submitted electronically by midnight Cambridge, Massachusetts time.

November 21, 2026: Deadline for the two online letters of recommendation.

Because the recommendation deadline comes after the main application deadline, applicants should contact their referees well in advance rather than waiting until the application deadline approaches.

Final Checklist Before Applying

Before submitting an application, prospective applicants should make sure that they:

  • Hold a PhD at the time of application.
  • Have a scan of their PhD certificate ready to upload.
  • Are not pursuing a second PhD.
  • Have a project directly relevant to the fellowship’s research scope.
  • Can conduct most of their research in Florence.
  • Are conversant in English.
  • Have familiarity with Italian.
  • Understand that the fellowship is residential.
  • Can live in the Florence area and spend at least three days each week at the center.
  • Are prepared to work exclusively on the proposed project.
  • Do not plan to take on teaching or other obligations during the fellowship.
  • Have identified two scholars who can provide recommendations.
  • Have registered their referees early enough for them to submit their recommendations.
  • Have selected their preferred fall or winter-spring term.
  • Have considered visa, residence permit, and health coverage requirements.
  • Have disclosed any partial salary or outside grant support where applicable.
  • Are applying for only one type of I Tatti fellowship during the academic year.
  • Submit the application before November 16, 2026.
  • Ensure both recommendation letters are submitted by November 21, 2026.

Conclusion

The Wallace Fellowship at Harvard’s I Tatti provides a highly focused residential research opportunity for scholars investigating the historiography and continuing impact of the Italian Renaissance in the modern era.

With a monthly grant of USD 5,200, a relocation supplement of up to USD 1,800, potential housing support, access to the Biblioteca Berenson, and participation in the scholarly community at I Tatti, the fellowship is structured to give selected researchers substantial time and resources to advance an important academic project.

The fellowship welcomes scholars from all nations and supports interdisciplinary research spanning art, architecture, history, literature, material culture, music, philosophy, religion, science, and other fields connected to the Renaissance and modernity.

Prospective applicants should pay particular attention to the research proposal, as the selection committee places significant emphasis on the strength of the proposed project, its potential to produce original results, the applicant’s curriculum vitae, and the candidate’s potential contribution to the intellectual life of the Harvard Center.

Interested scholars should begin preparing early, particularly because two recommendation letters are required. The main application deadline is November 16, 2026, while recommendation letters must be submitted by November 21, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Aspiring entrepreneurs and newly established business owners can now apply for the Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs programme, a European business exchange initiative that enables participants to learn directly from experienced entrepreneurs in another participating country.

Unlike a traditional classroom course, employment position or student mobility programme, Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs connects two individual entrepreneurs for a practical period of business collaboration. A new or aspiring entrepreneur spends between one and six months working alongside an experienced host entrepreneur, gaining first-hand knowledge of business development, management, finance, marketing, customer relations and international expansion.

The programme is financed by the European Commission and implemented with the assistance of approved local contact points, including chambers of commerce, start-up centres, incubators and other business-support organisations. Application and participation are free of charge. According to the official programme website, the exchange is partly financed through financial assistance provided to eligible new entrepreneurs.

Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs 2026 at a Glance

  • Programme name: Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs
  • Programme funder: European Commission
  • Programme management: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency
  • Exchange duration: One to six months
  • Exchange format: Entrepreneur-to-entrepreneur business collaboration
  • Location: Another participating country
  • Financial support: Monthly country-based financial assistance for eligible new entrepreneurs
  • Host entrepreneur funding: No European funding is provided to hosts
  • Application fee: None
  • Participation fee: None
  • Application deadline: No deadline; applications are accepted throughout the year
  • Business sectors: All sectors may be considered
  • Minimum age: Participants must be over 18
  • Official application portal: Apply through the Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs IT platform

What Is Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs?

Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs is an international business mobility programme created to support people who are planning to establish a business or have recently started one.

The programme helps aspiring and early-stage entrepreneurs develop the practical skills required to establish and manage a sustainable small or medium-sized enterprise. Instead of receiving only theoretical instruction, participants work directly with an experienced entrepreneur in another country.

During the exchange, the new entrepreneur observes how an established business operates while contributing their own knowledge, skills, ideas and understanding of their home market. The collaboration is intended to create benefits for both parties.

The new entrepreneur may gain practical business experience, improve a business plan, understand a foreign market and develop international contacts. The host entrepreneur may receive new ideas, specialised knowledge, access to another market and opportunities for future international cooperation.

The exchange can also lead to longer-term commercial relationships, including:

  • Joint ventures
  • Contractor and supplier relationships
  • Cross-border partnerships
  • Market-entry cooperation
  • Product development
  • Business referrals
  • Subcontracting arrangements
  • Continued professional collaboration

However, any future relationship must remain separate from the purpose and approval of the original exchange. The programme will not approve arrangements where a pre-existing commercial or personal relationship makes programme support unnecessary.

Who Can Participate as a New Entrepreneur?

Applicants may participate as new entrepreneurs if they fall within one of the following situations:

  1. They are firmly planning to establish their own business and have developed a viable business plan; or
  2. They have already established a business but have less than three years of total entrepreneurial experience.

The business may operate in any sector. There is no restriction requiring applicants to work in technology, manufacturing or another particular industry.

New entrepreneurs must also:

  • Be over 18 years of age
  • Be permanently resident in an eligible EU Member State or participating Single Market Programme country
  • Have a concrete business idea or project supported by a proper business plan
  • Be motivated to learn from an experienced entrepreneur in another participating country
  • Be prepared to contribute useful skills, knowledge and competencies to the host business
  • Be willing to participate actively throughout the agreed exchange
  • Have sufficient language ability to communicate and collaborate with the proposed host
  • Be prepared to supplement the programme’s financial assistance if it does not cover every expense
  • Personally submit the application through the official programme platform
  • Participate in the programme as a new entrepreneur only once

The programme’s official eligibility requirements are available on the new entrepreneur profile page.

Who Can Participate as a Host Entrepreneur?

Experienced business owners can apply to host an aspiring or newly established entrepreneur.

A host entrepreneur must:

  • Be permanently resident in a participating country
  • Have a company registered in that participating country
  • Be the owner-manager of a micro, small or medium-sized enterprise; or
  • Be directly involved in entrepreneurship at the board level of an SME rather than serving only as an employee
  • Have more than three years of experience operating a business as an entrepreneur
  • Be willing to share business knowledge and experience
  • Be prepared to mentor the visiting new entrepreneur
  • Provide a genuine learning and entrepreneurial collaboration
  • Sign the programme’s Commitment to Quality
  • Complete an online feedback questionnaire after the exchange

The host must ensure that the visiting entrepreneur receives meaningful business exposure. The programme must not be used to obtain unpaid labour, recruit an intern or fill an ordinary employee position. Full host requirements are explained on the official host entrepreneur profile page.

What Qualifies as a Small or Medium-Sized Enterprise?

Host businesses are generally expected to comply with the European Union definition of a micro, small or medium-sized enterprise.

The main thresholds are:

  • Micro-enterprise: Fewer than 10 employees and annual turnover or balance-sheet total not exceeding €2 million
  • Small enterprise: Fewer than 50 employees and annual turnover or balance-sheet total not exceeding €10 million
  • Medium-sized enterprise: Fewer than 250 employees and annual turnover not exceeding €50 million or a balance-sheet total not exceeding €43 million

The legal form of the business is not necessarily decisive. Independent professionals, self-employed individuals, eligible cooperatives, foundations, associations and certain non-profit organisations may potentially participate if they conduct an economic activity and satisfy the programme’s SME and entrepreneurial requirements.

Participating Countries

Residency requirements differ for new entrepreneurs and host entrepreneurs.

New entrepreneurs must be permanently resident in an EU Member State or a participating Single Market Programme third country.

Eligible EU Member States include:

  • Austria
  • Belgium
  • Bulgaria
  • Croatia
  • Cyprus
  • Czechia
  • Denmark
  • Estonia
  • Finland
  • France
  • Germany
  • Greece
  • Hungary
  • Ireland
  • Italy
  • Latvia
  • Lithuania
  • Luxembourg
  • Malta
  • Netherlands
  • Poland
  • Portugal
  • Romania
  • Slovakia
  • Slovenia
  • Spain
  • Sweden

Participating Single Market Programme third countries currently listed by the programme include:

  • Albania
  • Bosnia and Herzegovina
  • Iceland
  • Kosovo
  • Liechtenstein
  • Moldova
  • Montenegro
  • North Macedonia
  • Norway
  • Serbia
  • Türkiye
  • Ukraine

Host entrepreneurs may also be based in the following participating non-Single Market Programme destinations:

  • Canada
  • Singapore
  • United Kingdom
  • United States

Entrepreneurs from EU outermost regions and eligible Overseas Countries and Territories may also participate under the programme’s applicable rules.

Applicants should consult the current official list of participating countries before applying because programme participation and destination availability may change.

How Permanent Residence Is Determined

Eligibility is based primarily on permanent residence rather than nationality.

For an applicant with a registered company, permanent residence is generally treated as the country where that company is registered. Where a company operates through establishments in more than one participating country, the entrepreneur should select the country where they are personally based.

If the applicant does not have a registered company, permanent residence is normally the country where the applicant has spent at least 183 days during the previous 12 months.

An applicant currently living in a non-participating country will normally be considered ineligible, even if that person may satisfy other elements of the residence definition. The detailed residence rules are available in the programme’s permanent residence guidance.

Duration and Structure of the Exchange

An approved Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs exchange can last from one to six months.

The exchange may take place as one continuous stay or may be divided into shorter weekly periods. Where the exchange is divided into separate periods, all approved periods must generally be completed within an overall timeframe of no more than 12 months.

The final duration is agreed between the new entrepreneur and the host entrepreneur and must be approved by their respective local contact points. Acceptance of an initial application does not automatically guarantee a particular host, destination, duration or amount of funding.

The exchange must take place in another participating country. A new entrepreneur cannot complete the exchange in their own country of residence.

What Can Participants Do During the Exchange?

The precise activities are agreed between the new and host entrepreneurs and documented in their activity plan.

Activities may include:

  • Working alongside and shadowing the experienced host entrepreneur
  • Studying the host company’s daily management systems
  • Conducting market research
  • Identifying new commercial opportunities
  • Exploring international or cross-border markets
  • Supporting entrepreneurship-development projects
  • Participating in innovation and research-related activities
  • Improving the new entrepreneur’s business plan
  • Learning about business finance and financial management
  • Studying customer relationship systems
  • Understanding pricing and sales strategies
  • Reviewing branding and marketing practices
  • Exploring supply chains, operations and business partnerships
  • Developing new products, services or international business concepts
  • Learning about the regulatory and cultural environment of another participating country

The exchange should have clear learning objectives for the new entrepreneur and identifiable business value for the host.

Benefits for New Entrepreneurs

New entrepreneurs can gain practical knowledge that may be difficult to obtain through academic study alone.

Potential benefits include:

  • Up to six months of practical learning with an experienced business owner
  • Improved understanding of how to establish and manage an SME
  • Exposure to marketing, sales, accounting, customer relations and business finance
  • An opportunity to test and strengthen a business plan
  • Greater confidence in making entrepreneurial decisions
  • Development of management, technical and sector-specific skills
  • Better understanding of international and European markets
  • Experience of different organisational and business cultures
  • Improved foreign-language and communication skills
  • Access to a network of international entrepreneurs
  • Opportunities to identify future business partners
  • Potential development of cross-border commercial cooperation
  • Greater awareness of foreign customers, competitors and regulatory conditions
  • Financial assistance toward eligible travel and living costs

More information is available on the programme’s benefits for new entrepreneurs page.

Benefits for Host Entrepreneurs

Host entrepreneurs do not receive European financial assistance for hosting. However, the programme can provide significant commercial and professional value.

Benefits may include:

  • Working with a motivated entrepreneur who brings new ideas and perspectives
  • Accessing skills or specialised knowledge that may not already exist in the host company
  • Receiving fresh observations about the company’s products, services or processes
  • Learning about the new entrepreneur’s home market
  • Identifying opportunities for international expansion
  • Developing cross-border contacts
  • Finding potential future business partners
  • Strengthening the company’s international network
  • Improving communication and foreign-language skills
  • Acting as a mentor and contributing to entrepreneurship development
  • Increasing the company’s international visibility
  • Exploring future joint ventures, supply relationships or other cooperation

The programme emphasises mutual value: the host provides experience and guidance, while the new entrepreneur contributes ideas, knowledge and practical support. Further details are available on the benefits for host entrepreneurs page.

Financial Support for New Entrepreneurs

Eligible new entrepreneurs may receive financial assistance toward the cost of travelling to and living in the host country.

The assistance:

  • Is paid by the new entrepreneur’s selected local contact point
  • Is governed by a financial agreement between the entrepreneur and the local contact point
  • Is normally calculated according to a monthly lump sum
  • Depends on the country where the exchange takes place
  • Covers only the approved period spent abroad collaborating with the host
  • Is intended to contribute toward travel, accommodation and subsistence expenses
  • May be paid in several instalments under the signed agreement
  • May not cover every cost of the exchange
  • May need to be supplemented with the participant’s own resources

Host entrepreneurs do not receive European funding under the programme.

The official financial-assistance table currently linked by the programme applies to exchanges beginning on or after 1 June 2024. The listed monthly amounts for currently participating destinations are:

Monthly amount Country or category
€600 Albania and Ukraine
€650 Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Kosovo, Lithuania, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania and Serbia
€700 Hungary, Latvia, Moldova and Slovakia
€750 Czechia and Malta
€800 Croatia, Estonia, Slovenia and Türkiye
€850 Cyprus, Greece and Portugal
€900 Belgium, Germany, Luxembourg and Spain
€950 France and the Netherlands
€1,000 Austria, Finland, Iceland, Italy and Sweden
€1,050 Canada
€1,100 Ireland and the United Kingdom
€1,150 Singapore
€1,200 Denmark, Liechtenstein, Norway and the United States
€1,200 Eligible participants travelling from or to EU outermost regions and Overseas Countries and Territories
€1,200 Entrepreneurs with disabilities, regardless of the destination

Applicants should treat these figures as contribution rates rather than a promise that all actual costs will be fully covered. The final amount, payment schedule and financial conditions will be established in the agreement with the relevant intermediary organisation. Applicants should verify the latest official monthly financial-assistance table before making travel or accommodation commitments.

Application Documents for New Entrepreneurs

New entrepreneurs should prepare the following before starting their online application:

  1. Curriculum Vitae

The CV should provide a clear and current summary of the applicant’s:

  • Education
  • Professional experience
  • Entrepreneurial experience
  • Technical competencies
  • Management capabilities
  • Business and sector knowledge

The Europass CV format is preferred but is not compulsory. English is strongly encouraged because it can make the applicant’s profile easier for intermediary organisations and potential hosts to understand.

  1. Motivation Statement

The motivation section should explain:

  • Why the applicant wants to join the programme
  • What business knowledge they hope to acquire
  • Why an international exchange is relevant to their business
  • What skills they can contribute to the host company
  • How the exchange will strengthen their planned or recently established business
  • What practical results they expect to achieve
  • How they will apply the experience after returning home

A generic motivation statement is unlikely to be competitive. It should demonstrate commitment, initiative, seriousness, creativity and clearly defined learning needs.

  1. Full Business Plan

A full business plan is compulsory for new entrepreneurs. A brief idea alone is not sufficient.

The business plan should include at least:

  • A clear description of the proposed product or service
  • The problem or customer need addressed
  • A definition of the target market
  • Market-size and demand considerations
  • Competitor analysis
  • Marketing and sales strategy
  • Operational requirements
  • Estimated expenses and revenue for the following two years
  • Break-even analysis
  • The applicant’s implementation strategy

The programme does not prescribe a single business-plan template. However, the selected local contact point will assess whether the document is sufficiently complete, viable and professionally prepared.

The full business plan is treated as a confidential document and is generally accessible only to the applicant, the selected intermediary organisation, the programme Support Office and the European Commission.

  1. Business Plan Summary

Applicants must also submit a shorter summary of their business plan. The registration guide indicates a maximum length of 2,000 characters.

Unlike the full confidential business plan, the summary may be visible to accepted entrepreneurs and intermediary organisations in the programme’s online catalogue. Applicants should therefore avoid including trade secrets or other sensitive information.

  1. Language Information

Applicants must be able to communicate effectively with their proposed host. The programme does not provide language training.

There is no universal language examination requirement, but applicants should be comfortable speaking, understanding, reading and writing in the language used during the exchange. The registration guide refers to approximately B2-level ability as a useful benchmark. English is strongly encouraged because it is widely understood across the programme.

  1. Geographical and Sector Preferences

Applicants are asked to identify:

  • Their principal business sector
  • Additional sectors relevant to the planned exchange
  • Their preferred host country
  • Alternative destination countries
  • Their proposed exchange duration
  • The periods during which they are available

Flexibility regarding destinations and dates can increase the likelihood of finding a suitable host.

The complete preparation requirements are explained in the official registration guide for new entrepreneurs.

How to Apply for Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs

The application and matching process generally involves the following stages:

Step 1: Check Your Eligibility

Determine whether you qualify as a new entrepreneur or an experienced host entrepreneur. Confirm your permanent-residence status and ensure that your country is currently participating.

Step 2: Identify a Local Contact Point

Select an approved intermediary organisation that operates in your country or region of residence. The organisation will guide you through assessment, matching, preparation and implementation.

Applicants living in an eligible country without an active local contact point may be able to select an intermediary organisation in another participating European country.

Step 3: Prepare the Required Documents

New entrepreneurs should prepare their CV, motivation statement, complete business plan and business-plan summary.

Host entrepreneurs should prepare a detailed professional and company profile, explain their motivation for hosting and identify the skills or experience they can offer.

Step 4: Submit the Online Application Personally

Applications must be submitted through the official programme platform. Participants must not allow an external organisation or third party to submit an application on their behalf.

The official Apply Now page also provides access to explanatory material, registration guides and a preview of the online form.

Step 5: Application Assessment

The selected intermediary organisation reviews the application for eligibility, completeness and quality.

The new entrepreneur registration guide indicates that an initial check should normally be conducted within two weeks of receiving the application. The application may be:

  • Accepted
  • Placed on hold pending additional information
  • Returned to the applicant
  • Refused

If information is missing, the applicant may be asked to provide it within a specified period. Acceptance gives the participant access to the programme’s online catalogue but does not by itself guarantee an exchange.

Step 6: Find a Suitable Entrepreneur

Accepted participants can pursue a match in two ways:

  1. Suggest an eligible entrepreneur with whom they are already in contact, subject to the programme’s restrictions; or
  2. Search the online catalogue with support from the local contact point.

The proposed host should be relevant to the new entrepreneur’s business objectives and capable of providing genuine entrepreneurial learning.

Step 7: Agree on the Exchange Plan

The two entrepreneurs must agree on:

  • Exchange dates
  • Duration
  • Learning objectives
  • Proposed activities
  • Expected contributions from each participant
  • Anticipated business outcomes

These details must be submitted to the local contact points for assessment and approval.

Step 8: Sign the Required Agreements

All parties digitally sign a Commitment to Quality setting out the objectives and activity plan.

The new entrepreneur also signs a financial agreement with the intermediary organisation. This agreement specifies the funding, responsibilities, payment arrangements, timetable and relevant legal conditions.

Step 9: Complete the Exchange

The new entrepreneur travels to the host country and participates in the agreed activities. Financial assistance is provided according to the signed agreement.

Step 10: Submit Feedback

After the exchange, both entrepreneurs must complete the required feedback questionnaires. The new entrepreneur should explain the activities completed, knowledge acquired and effect of the exchange on their business development.

The complete official process is available on the How to Participate page.

Activities and Relationships That Are Not Permitted

Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs is not an internship, employment scheme or source of unpaid labour.

Proposed exchanges may be rejected where:

  • The host intends to use the new entrepreneur as an ordinary employee or intern
  • The parties already have a professional relationship that makes programme support unnecessary
  • The host is already, or plans to become, a co-owner or investor in the new entrepreneur’s business
  • The new entrepreneur intends to establish a branch of the host’s business
  • The parties are close relatives, spouses or partners
  • A significant personal relationship creates a conflict of interest
  • The new entrepreneur has already worked at the host’s business through another programme
  • The exchange provides no clear additional value to both businesses
  • The application is submitted by a third party
  • Financial assistance is used for a purpose unrelated to the approved exchange

One host entrepreneur cannot host more than one new entrepreneur at the same time. Where co-founders from the same company participate as hosts, their exchanges must take place at different times.

Application Deadline

There is no fixed deadline to register for Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs.

The programme accepts online applications throughout the year, according to its official deadline guidance.

Applicants should nevertheless apply early. The assessment, matching, approval and contracting stages can require considerable time, and the availability and budgets of intermediary organisations may affect when an exchange can begin.

Application Cost

Application and participation are completely free of charge.

No intermediary organisation, consultant or external party should charge an applicant an application or participation fee. Applicants must use the official platform and submit their information personally.

Technical Requirements for Applying

The online application system is designed to work with the latest versions of:

  • Microsoft Edge
  • Google Chrome
  • Mozilla Firefox

Applicants should use a reliable email address that they expect to retain, because the registered email address, first name and last name may not be changeable after registration.

Official Application and Contact Information

Official information page: Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs – Apply Now

Online application portal: Start an Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs application

Local contact points: Find an intermediary organisation

Support Office email: support@erasmus-entrepreneurs.eu

Support Office telephone: +32 2 282 08 73

Practical Tips for a Strong Application

  • Prepare a complete business plan with realistic financial assumptions.
  • Clearly explain what you need to learn from an experienced entrepreneur.
  • Describe the specific skills and knowledge you can contribute to the host.
  • Link every proposed exchange objective to the development of your own business.
  • Use a professional and updated CV, preferably in English.
  • Avoid vague statements about wanting international exposure.
  • Select host countries and business sectors that genuinely match your plans.
  • Remain flexible about dates and alternative destinations.
  • Prepare a personal budget because the financial assistance may not cover every expense.
  • Do not disclose commercially sensitive information in the public business-plan summary.
  • Apply only through the official programme portal.
  • Never pay an application or participation fee.
  • Do not describe the proposed exchange as an internship or employment placement.

Conclusion

Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs offers aspiring founders and newly established business owners an opportunity to gain practical international business experience while learning directly from an experienced entrepreneur.

Through a structured exchange lasting between one and six months, new entrepreneurs can strengthen their business plans, develop management skills, explore international markets and establish valuable professional relationships. Experienced host entrepreneurs can benefit from fresh ideas, specialised knowledge and access to potential markets and partners abroad.

The programme is free to join, accepts applications throughout the year and provides eligible new entrepreneurs with country-based financial assistance toward travel and living expenses. Applicants should carefully confirm their residency eligibility, prepare a serious business plan and submit a clear application demonstrating both what they expect to learn and what they can contribute.

For more global opportunities, click HERE.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for the 2027 intake of the Joint Master of Science in Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security, an international postgraduate programme jointly offered by the United Nations University Institute for Environment and Human Security and the Department of Geography at the University of Bonn.

The two-year, full-time programme is delivered in Bonn, Germany, and combines advanced academic study with practical training in environmental risks, climate change, disaster management, human security, vulnerability, resilience and sustainable development.

A limited number of fully funded scholarships are available through the German Academic Exchange Service’s Development-Related Postgraduate Courses programme, commonly known as DAAD EPOS. These scholarships are intended for qualified professionals from eligible developing and emerging countries who have relevant postgraduate work experience and plan to continue working as development practitioners after completing the degree.

Applications for the October 2027 intake must be completed by 31 October 2026 at 23:59 Central European Time. Both the online application and the complete application documents submitted by email must be received before the deadline.

Programme Summary

  • Programme: Joint Master of Science in Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security
  • Institutions: United Nations University Institute for Environment and Human Security and University of Bonn
  • Degree level: Master of Science
  • Programme location: Bonn, Germany
  • Study format: Full-time and residential
  • Programme duration: Two years
  • Normal study period: Four semesters
  • Programme start: October 2027
  • Application opening date: 31 July 2026
  • Application deadline: 31 October 2026 at 23:59 CET
  • Teaching language: English
  • Minimum English level: B2
  • Recommended English level: C1
  • Tuition fees: None
  • University semester contribution: Approximately €310 per semester
  • Additional UNU contribution: €100 for each of the first three semesters
  • Scholarship opportunity: Limited fully funded DAAD EPOS scholarships
  • Compulsory internship: At least eight weeks
  • Application method: Online form followed by submission of application documents by email
  • Application email: master-georisk@ehs.unu.edu
  • Official programme page: Joint MSc in Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security
  • Online application: Start the 2027 programme application

About the Joint Master’s Programme

The Joint MSc in Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security was developed to provide postgraduate students with the theoretical knowledge, research methods and practical tools necessary to understand environmental risks and their consequences for societies.

The programme examines how natural hazards and environmental changes emerge, how they affect human-nature relationships and why certain communities, regions and population groups are more vulnerable than others.

Students investigate concepts such as:

  • Environmental risk
  • Natural hazards
  • Human security
  • Social and environmental vulnerability
  • Community and institutional resilience
  • Climate change adaptation
  • Disaster risk reduction
  • Risk governance
  • Sustainable development
  • Human-nature relationships
  • Humanitarian response
  • Earth system science
  • Environmental policy

The programme combines the academic strengths of the University of Bonn’s Department of Geography with the applied, policy-oriented and international research environment of UNU-EHS.

This collaboration enables students to study environmental risks from both physical and human geography perspectives while connecting their academic learning to international development, policymaking and humanitarian practice.

The official 2027 call for applications highlights the programme’s strong interest in environmental risk governance, human-nature relations and challenges facing the Global South.

Main Objectives of the Programme

The programme aims to:

  • Develop advanced theoretical and methodological expertise in environmental risks and human security
  • Connect academic knowledge with practical experience
  • Examine vulnerability, resilience and adaptation in different geographical contexts
  • Maintain a strong focus on developing countries and the Global South
  • Create an intercultural and interdisciplinary learning environment
  • Strengthen students’ qualitative and quantitative research capabilities
  • Develop competence in geographical information systems and remote sensing
  • Provide opportunities to participate in research projects at UNU-EHS and the University of Bonn
  • Facilitate interaction with the United Nations system and other international organisations
  • Prepare graduates for professional careers in development, climate adaptation, disaster risk reduction, humanitarian work, environmental governance and related fields

Academic Areas Covered by the Programme

The programme brings together a wide range of fields and research interests, including:

  • Vulnerability assessment
  • Ecosystem services
  • Sustainable development
  • Disaster management
  • Disaster risk reduction
  • Climate change adaptation
  • Human-nature relationships
  • Science and technology studies
  • Development geography
  • Geomorphology
  • Socio-hydrology
  • Future studies
  • Geographic information systems
  • Remote sensing
  • Risk management
  • Human security
  • Risk forecasting and prediction
  • Humanitarian response
  • Environmental policy and governance

This combination allows students to evaluate environmental risks as interconnected physical, social, political, technological and economic challenges.

Programme Curriculum and Modules

The Joint MSc consists of 12 modules. Ten modules are principally taught during the first three semesters. The programme then includes a compulsory internship, a master’s colloquium and independent work on the master’s thesis.

Major modules include:

  1. Theories and Concepts of Risk

This module introduces the central theories and conceptual approaches used to understand environmental risks, hazards, vulnerability, resilience and human security.

  1. General Approaches to Risk and Human Security

Students examine new approaches to development geography and Earth system science, connecting social and physical processes.

  1. Research Methods

This module develops the methodological skills required to design, conduct and evaluate interdisciplinary research.

  1. Academic Writing and Intercultural Skills

Students strengthen academic communication, structured scientific writing and intercultural collaboration.

  1. Advanced Debates on Risk and Human Security

The module examines contemporary academic and policy debates surrounding environmental change, social vulnerability and human security.

  1. Research Seminar

Students participate in applied research and project-based work connected to environmental risks and human security.

  1. Academic Presentation and Communication Skills

This module develops the ability to present complex scientific findings clearly to academic, professional and policy audiences.

  1. Risk Management in the Context of Climate Change

Students study climate-related risks, adaptation strategies, governance arrangements and practical risk-management approaches.

  1. Disaster Management and Humanitarian Response

The programme examines disaster preparedness, emergency response, humanitarian systems and disaster risk reduction.

  1. Field Trips

Students participate in field-based learning activities lasting at least three days and prepare an associated report.

  1. Compulsory Internship

Students must complete an internship of at least eight weeks. The internship must be directly connected to the subject matter of the programme.

Students receive support in searching for suitable opportunities, but the programme does not automatically place students with an internship host.

  1. Master’s Colloquium and Thesis

Students develop and present their research proposal through the master’s colloquium before completing an independent master’s thesis.

The thesis carries 30 credit points and is normally completed over six months. Students must have earned at least 60 credit points before beginning the thesis.

The current programme structure can be reviewed in the official curriculum overview.

General Academic Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must hold a first higher education qualification, normally a bachelor’s degree or an equivalent recognised qualification, in Geography or a closely related and relevant academic discipline.

The selection committee reviews all academic achievements, including:

  • Bachelor’s-level coursework
  • Any completed master’s-level coursework
  • Exchange-semester credits
  • Summer schools
  • Additional university courses
  • Other recognised academic studies

The majority of the applicant’s completed coursework must relate to the following three areas:

1. Human Geography and Social Sciences

Relevant subjects should focus on topics such as:

  • Spatial patterns
  • Society
  • Development
  • Human geography
  • Population and settlement
  • Social vulnerability
  • Regional development
  • Human-environment relationships

2. Scientific Methodology and Empirical Research

Applicants should have studied research-related subjects, including:

  • Scientific research design
  • Qualitative methods
  • Quantitative methods
  • Data collection
  • Statistical or empirical analysis
  • Field research
  • Academic writing
  • Research methodology

3. Physical Geography, Geosciences and Environmental Sciences

Relevant coursework should address areas such as:

  • Earth system science
  • Physical geography
  • Environmental systems
  • Geosciences
  • Climate processes
  • Natural hazards
  • Ecosystems
  • Environmental change

Applicants should carefully compare their academic transcripts with these three areas before applying. The final decision regarding the relevance and adequacy of previous academic study can only be made by the programme’s selection committee after reviewing the complete application.

Applicants Who May Not Be Eligible

The programme is not principally designed for applicants whose academic background is dominated by engineering subjects.

Graduates of International Relations or similar programmes will generally not be considered unless their academic profile has a strong and demonstrable connection with environmental risks.

Current PhD students and people who already hold a PhD are not eligible for this master’s programme.

Applicants with multidisciplinary degrees should not rely only on the title of their qualification. Their transcripts must show that most of their academic coursework is relevant to human geography, research methods and environmental or Earth system sciences.

Can Final-Year Bachelor’s Students Apply?

Applicants who will complete their bachelor’s degree after the application deadline may submit an application using their current transcripts.

If admitted, they must subsequently provide their final transcript and bachelor’s degree certificate. The qualifying degree must be completed before the Joint MSc begins in October 2027.

Motivation Requirements

Applicants must demonstrate a strong and genuine motivation to contribute to the fields of human security, environmental change and risk management.

The programme seeks applicants who are:

  • Interested in interdisciplinary research
  • Prepared to study in a multicultural academic environment
  • Motivated to address environmental and development challenges
  • Capable of connecting scientific knowledge with practical solutions
  • Interested in environmental risks affecting developing countries and the Global South
  • Able to explain how the programme relates to their future career

The required programme motivation letter must specifically address:

  • The applicant’s academic background
  • Relevant professional experience
  • Knowledge of the programme curriculum
  • Particular scientific interests
  • Future career aspirations
  • How the programme will support those aspirations
  • The applicant’s suitability for the programme

Applicants currently enrolled in another postgraduate programme must explain why they intend to leave or change their existing programme.

English-Language Requirements

The programme is taught in English. Applicants must demonstrate at least B2 proficiency under the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, although C1 proficiency is recommended.

Merely completing a degree taught in English does not automatically exempt an applicant from submitting a recognised language certificate.

The following tests and minimum results are accepted:

English test Minimum score
TOEFL Paper-Based Test 550
TOEFL Internet-Based Test 79
TOEFL Computer-Based Test 213
IELTS Academic 6.5
Cambridge Advanced English At least B2
Cambridge Proficiency in English Accepted
telc English B2–C1
Pearson Test of English Academic 67
Duolingo English Test 120

Native English speakers from the following countries are exempt from providing a language certificate:

  • Australia
  • Canada
  • Republic of Ireland
  • New Zealand
  • United Kingdom
  • United States

German applicants who completed the relevant advanced English course through the “Leistungskurs Abitur” may provide suitable documentation in place of one of the listed tests.

Applicants should consult the official programme requirements and FAQs before selecting or booking an English test.

DAAD EPOS Fully Funded Scholarship

The Joint MSc is among the selected development-related postgraduate programmes supported through the DAAD EPOS funding scheme.

A limited number of fully funded scholarships may be awarded to highly qualified applicants from eligible developing and emerging countries.

Admission to the master’s programme does not guarantee a DAAD EPOS scholarship. Applicants can be admitted academically without receiving funding and may then choose to enrol as self-funded students.

DAAD EPOS Scholarship Benefits

According to the current DAAD EPOS scholarship information, funding for graduate-level scholarship holders may include:

  • A monthly scholarship payment of €992
  • Payments toward health insurance
  • Payments toward accident insurance
  • Personal liability insurance coverage
  • A travel allowance, unless travel costs are covered by another source

Depending on individual circumstances, recipients may also receive:

  • A monthly rent subsidy
  • An allowance for accompanying family members

Applicants should consult the current DAAD call and their eventual scholarship award documents for the final financial conditions.

Additional DAAD EPOS Eligibility Requirements

Candidates seeking the DAAD EPOS scholarship must satisfy the general academic requirements of the master’s programme and the following additional conditions:

  • Be from an eligible developing or emerging country
  • Hold an appropriate bachelor’s degree
  • Have strong academic results, normally placing them within the upper third of their graduating group
  • Have accumulated at least two years of relevant professional experience after completing the bachelor’s degree
  • Complete the required two years of experience by the application deadline
  • Have obtained their most recent academic degree no more than six years before the application deadline
  • Not already hold another master’s degree in a similar field
  • Intend to pursue a practitioner-oriented career in development after graduation
  • Not use the scholarship principally as preparation for an academic career or PhD
  • Demonstrate development-related motivation
  • Be prepared to take social responsibility and support positive change in their professional environment
  • Commit fully to completing the Joint MSc if selected
  • Normally not have lived in Germany for more than 15 months by the application deadline

Relevant professional experience may have been acquired through:

  • A government organisation
  • A public authority
  • A non-governmental organisation
  • A state-owned organisation
  • A private company
  • A development agency
  • Another professional institution working in a relevant field

Only work experience obtained after completion of the bachelor’s degree is counted toward the two-year requirement. Experience accumulated after the application deadline cannot be included.

Tuition Fees and Other Study Charges

There are no tuition fees for the Joint MSc.

Students are nevertheless required to pay certain institutional contributions:

  • Approximately €310 per semester to the University of Bonn, including the local public-transportation ticket
  • €100 to UNU for each of the first three semesters

These amounts do not include accommodation, food, personal expenses, visa costs or other living expenses in Bonn. Institutional contributions may also change before enrolment.

The programme is full-time and residential. It cannot be completed remotely or on a part-time basis, and students must live in or near Bonn so they can attend classes.

Documents Required from All Applicants

Applicants must arrange their documents in the exact order prescribed by the programme.

1. Online Application Confirmation

After completing the online application form, applicants will receive confirmation by email. This confirmation must be signed, dated and included as a scanned document in the application package.

2. Programme Motivation Letter

The motivation letter must:

  • Be between one and two pages
  • Be dated
  • Explain the applicant’s academic and professional suitability
  • Demonstrate knowledge of the programme
  • Identify specific scientific interests
  • Explain future career aspirations
  • Describe how the programme will benefit the applicant

3. Europass Curriculum Vitae

The CV must:

  • Use the Europass format
  • Be arranged in reverse chronological order
  • Not exceed three pages
  • Be signed and dated
  • Include exact dates
  • Correspond precisely with the dates appearing in supporting references and certificates

4. Academic Degree Certificates

Applicants should submit:

  • Bachelor’s degree certificate or equivalent
  • Master’s degree certificate, if available
  • Certified translations where documents are not in English or German

DAAD EPOS applicants must ensure that the original academic certificate has been signed or stamped by the issuing university.

5. Academic Transcripts

Transcripts should cover the bachelor’s degree, any available master’s study and other relevant academic credits.

The transcripts must:

  • Be in English or German or accompanied by certified translations
  • Show an identifiable overall average grade
  • Include an explanation of the applicable grading system, except for German qualifications
  • Include relevant exchange semesters, summer schools and additional credits

For DAAD EPOS applicants, transcripts must be stamped by the issuing university or sent directly by the university registrar to master-georisk@ehs.unu.edu.

6. Proof of English Proficiency

Applicants must provide one of the accepted English-language certificates unless they qualify for a specified exemption.

7. Academic References

Academic references are recommended but optional.

Applicants may provide no more than two references from former university lecturers. Each reference should:

  • Be recent
  • Be dated
  • Be signed and stamped
  • Appear on official letterhead
  • Be written in English or German or accompanied by a certified translation

8. Passport Copy

Submit the passport page displaying the applicant’s name and personal information.

9. Other Relevant References

Applicants may submit up to three additional references covering relevant:

  • Employment
  • Internships
  • Professional training
  • Volunteering
  • Practical experience

School certificates should not be included.

10. APS Certificate Where Applicable

Applicants from China, India and Viet Nam must include a scan of their applicable Academic Evaluation Centre certificate.

Additional Documents for DAAD EPOS Applicants

Scholarship applicants must also include:

1. DAAD EPOS Checklist

The required checklist must be completed, dated and signed on the specified page. DAAD requires a handwritten signature; a digitally inserted signature is not accepted.

2. DAAD Application Form

The form must:

  • Be completed electronically rather than by hand
  • Be dated
  • Identify every EPOS programme for which the applicant is applying
  • List programme preferences in the required order

Applicants may normally apply for a maximum of three EPOS courses and must explain their priorities consistently.

3. Scholarship Motivation Letter

The scholarship motivation letter must be between one and two pages and must be dated.

It may build upon the general programme motivation letter, but it must additionally explain:

  • Why the applicant is seeking a DAAD scholarship
  • Why the applicant wants to study in Germany
  • How the application is related to development
  • How the scholarship will support the applicant’s professional ambitions
  • How the applicant expects to contribute as a development practitioner
  • The applicant’s programme preferences if applying to more than one EPOS course

4. Professional Reference from the Current Employer

The reference must:

  • Be recent
  • Be dated
  • Be signed and stamped
  • Be issued on official letterhead
  • Come from the employer, supervisor or human resources department
  • Be written in English or German or accompanied by a certified translation

5. Employment Certificates

The certificates must:

  • Document at least two years of relevant work experience after the bachelor’s degree
  • State the precise starting and ending dates in day-month-year format
  • Be issued by an authorised person
  • Be dated
  • Be signed and stamped
  • Appear on official letterhead

Mandatory Academic Writing Sample

Every applicant must submit a separate academic writing sample in English for the 2027 intake.

The essay should explain:

  1. How the applicant’s academic or professional experiences have influenced the subjects they want to explore during the master’s programme
  2. How those experiences could contribute to a possible master’s thesis
  3. Why the proposed perspective could help address an identifiable research gap

The writing sample must:

  • Be written as an academic essay
  • Be no longer than 1,000 words, excluding references
  • Draw upon relevant scientific literature
  • Use no more than 10 references
  • Follow APA referencing style
  • Be original work written personally by the applicant
  • Be submitted as a separate PDF
  • Include the required declaration of authenticity

The programme requires applicants to add the following declaration:

“I confirm to have written the essay myself, without the use of AI.”

The programme warns that plagiarism and artificial-intelligence checks may be applied. Applicants must therefore write the academic essay independently and should not submit AI-generated or plagiarised work.

Required Application Format

Applicants must comply with the following submission rules:

  • Complete the online application form first
  • Download or obtain the application confirmation sent by email
  • Sign and date the required confirmation
  • Submit the documents in the exact prescribed order
  • Merge the main documents into one PDF
  • Ensure the merged PDF does not exceed 8MB
  • Name the application file as: LastName.FirstName.pdf
  • Submit the academic writing sample as a separate PDF
  • Use a separate email for the writing sample if attachment limits make this necessary
  • Submit scans rather than smartphone photographs
  • Use certified translations where required
  • Do not send original documents
  • Do not send a paper application through the post
  • Ensure the complete package is received before the deadline

Applicants may be asked to present original certificates for verification after admission.

Step-by-Step Application Process

Step 1: Review the Eligibility Criteria

Check the programme requirements, academic subject requirements, English-language conditions and DAAD EPOS criteria where applicable.

Step 2: Complete the Online Application Form

Submit the official 2027 online application form.

The form can only be submitted once. Applicants who are not ready to complete it in one session should use the “Save and Continue Later” option.

Step 3: Receive and Sign the Confirmation

After submitting the online form, obtain the confirmation sent by email. Sign and date it as instructed.

Step 4: Prepare the Main Application Package

Arrange all required documents in the exact prescribed order and merge them into one PDF not exceeding 8MB.

Step 5: Prepare the Academic Writing Sample

Save the original academic essay as a separate PDF and include the required declaration of authenticity.

Step 6: Email the Application

Send the complete package to:

master-georisk@ehs.unu.edu

Both the online form and emailed application documents must be received by the deadline.

Applications sent directly to DAAD at the initial stage will not be forwarded to the programme.

Selection Process

The number of places is limited, and admission is regulated through a local Numerus Clausus selection process.

The selection committee considers:

  • Academic performance
  • Relevance of previous academic coursework
  • Research and methodological preparation
  • Ability to communicate at a scientific level
  • Quality of the academic writing sample
  • Motivation
  • Career plans
  • Relevant professional experience
  • Overall suitability for the programme

Formally complete applications are first assessed for academic eligibility.

Suitable candidates are expected to be shortlisted and invited to an interview in January or February 2027. The interview may assess their academic and professional background, motivation, career objectives and overall fit.

Candidates shortlisted for DAAD EPOS funding are subsequently forwarded to DAAD. The EPOS selection process is expected to take place between February and April.

Applicants are expected to receive a final update on their application status around April or May 2027.

An applicant who is admitted to the programme but is not awarded the DAAD EPOS scholarship may still accept the place as a self-funded student.

Can Admission Be Deferred?

Admission cannot be deferred to the following year.

An admitted applicant who cannot begin the programme in October 2027 will lose the place, which may be offered to another candidate on the waiting list. The applicant would need to submit a new application for a future intake.

Career Opportunities

Graduates can pursue careers in organisations working on environmental change, risk management, human security and international development.

Potential employers and sectors include:

  • United Nations agencies
  • International organisations
  • Government ministries and public authorities
  • Federal agencies
  • Development organisations
  • Humanitarian agencies
  • Non-governmental organisations
  • Research institutes
  • Universities and academic institutions
  • Environmental consultancies
  • Private companies
  • Disaster preparedness organisations
  • Climate change and sustainability programmes
  • Food-security organisations
  • Spatial-planning institutions
  • Environmental and development-policy bodies

Potential areas of work include:

  • Disaster risk reduction
  • Disaster preparedness
  • Humanitarian response
  • Climate change adaptation
  • Environmental risk assessment
  • Human security
  • Sustainable development
  • Vulnerability and resilience analysis
  • Environmental policy
  • Geographic information systems
  • Remote sensing
  • Food security
  • Spatial planning
  • Risk governance
  • International development
  • Research and policy analysis

Important Application Deadline

The application deadline for the October 2027 intake is:

31 October 2026 at 23:59 CET, Bonn, Germany time.

The application period runs from 31 July to 31 October 2026.

Late, incomplete and paper applications will not be considered. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day because the process requires both an online submission and a complete email application package.

Application Links and Contact Information

Official programme information: UNU-EHS Joint MSc in Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security

Online application form: Apply for the October 2027 intake

DAAD EPOS scholarship information: Development-Related Postgraduate Courses

Programme email: master-georisk@ehs.unu.edu

Conclusion

The Joint MSc in Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security provides an exceptional opportunity to study environmental risks, climate adaptation, disaster management and human security within the combined academic environments of the United Nations University and the University of Bonn.

Its interdisciplinary curriculum, research opportunities, compulsory internship and connection with the United Nations system make it particularly relevant for professionals seeking careers in environmental governance, disaster risk reduction, humanitarian response, international development and climate policy.

Applicants from eligible developing and emerging countries may also compete for a limited number of fully funded DAAD EPOS scholarships. Scholarship candidates must demonstrate strong academic performance, at least two years of relevant postgraduate professional experience, development-related motivation and a clear intention to continue working as practitioners after graduation.

Prospective candidates should examine their academic transcripts carefully, arrange their English-language evidence, prepare all certificates in the required format and write the mandatory academic essay independently. The complete online and email applications must reach the programme no later than 31 October 2026 at 23:59 CET.

For more global opportunities, click HERE.
