item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has announced an exciting international professional opportunity for an experienced economist to join its Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific in Bangkok, Thailand.

The UNDP Economist – Development Strategy position is designed for a highly experienced economics, development policy, research, or quantitative analysis professional who can contribute to evidence-based economic policy development, growth diagnostics, labour market analysis, inclusive growth strategies, structural transformation research, and government advisory work.

The position is particularly connected to UNDP’s Inclusive Growth Team and its Building Opportunities for Leadership in Development (BOLD) initiative, which supports governments in translating economic evidence, diagnostics, and foresight into practical and strategically prioritized development reforms.

This is a senior-level professional opportunity at IPSA-11 level, with a one-year contract and full-time schedule. The position is based in Bangkok, Thailand, and successful candidates will work closely with economists, policy specialists, UNDP Country Offices, government counterparts, development partners, research institutions, and other stakeholders across Asia and the Pacific.

For professionals with substantial experience in applied economic analysis and development policy, this opportunity provides the chance to contribute to major development strategy and economic transformation initiatives within the UN development system.

Opportunity Overview

The UNDP Economist – Development Strategy vacancy has the following key details:

  • Job Title: Economist – Development Strategy
  • Organization: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
  • Job Identification: 36454
  • Job Category: International professional job
  • Contract Type: International Personnel Service Agreement (IPSA)
  • Grade: IPSA-11
  • Duty Station: Bangkok, Thailand
  • Practice Area: Inclusive Growth
  • Bureau: Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific
  • Work Schedule: Full time
  • Contract Duration: 1 year
  • Required Language: English
  • Posting Date: 24 August 2026
  • Application Deadline: 9 September 2026 at 3:59 AM
  • Application Tier: Tier 0, Tier 1 and Tier 2 applicants
  • Education Requirement: Master’s degree with 7 years of relevant experience, or bachelor’s degree with 9 years of relevant experience
  • Primary Focus: Economic analysis, development strategy, inclusive growth, labour markets, productivity, inequality and structural transformation

About UNDP

The United Nations Development Programme is a major organization within the UN development system that works with countries and institutions to advance sustainable development and improve people’s lives.

UNDP operates at the intersection of development policy, institutional strengthening, economic transformation, poverty reduction, governance and the Sustainable Development Goals.

The organization uses research, policy advice, technical expertise and development partnerships to help countries address complex development challenges.

Through its Global Policy Network (GPN), UNDP connects international expertise with national and local priorities. This approach allows the organization to support governments in developing policies and institutional capabilities that can deliver sustainable and inclusive development outcomes.

The Economist – Development Strategy will therefore work within an environment where economic research and quantitative evidence are used to influence real-world development strategies.

About the Inclusive Growth Team

The position is located within the Inclusive Growth Team (IGT) at the UNDP Bangkok Regional Hub.

The team provides support to governments and UNDP Country Offices throughout Asia and the Pacific on economic and development-related challenges.

Its work includes analysing issues such as:

  • Economic growth
  • Productivity
  • Employment and job creation
  • Labour markets
  • Inequality
  • Poverty
  • Structural transformation
  • Social protection
  • Inclusive economic policies
  • Economic development strategies
  • Institutional capacity

The team combines economic research and policy expertise to help countries identify opportunities for sustainable and inclusive growth.

The successful Economist will contribute to this work by producing high-quality analysis, supporting policy discussions and helping translate complex economic evidence into practical recommendations.

What Is the BOLD Initiative?

A major component of the role is supporting Building Opportunities for Leadership in Development (BOLD).

BOLD is a UNDP high-level advisory initiative designed to help governments translate economic evidence, diagnostics and foresight into strategically prioritized reform pathways.

Rather than focusing only on producing economic research, the initiative seeks to connect analysis with government decision-making.

The Economist will therefore need to be capable of working with economic data while also understanding how evidence can be translated into development strategies and policy recommendations.

This makes the position particularly suitable for an economist who enjoys both technical research and policy-oriented work.

Key Responsibilities of the Economist – Development Strategy

The successful candidate will undertake a wide range of analytical, advisory, programme coordination and knowledge management responsibilities.

1. Conduct Technical Analysis and Research

One of the central responsibilities of the Economist will be conducting and supporting economic research under the BOLD initiative.

The successful candidate will be expected to analyse different aspects of economic development, including:

  • Economic growth
  • Structural transformation
  • Employment
  • Labour market trends
  • Productivity
  • Inequality
  • Inclusive development
  • Economic opportunities
  • Development policy

The Economist will use quantitative and qualitative research methods to produce economic diagnostics that can help governments and UNDP Country Offices understand development challenges and identify potential policy responses.

Growth and Development Diagnostics

The role requires experience or capability in conducting economic diagnostics.

This can involve examining why an economy is growing or underperforming, identifying structural constraints, assessing productivity and employment patterns, and determining which reforms could potentially improve economic outcomes.

The Economist may also support assessments of different economic sectors and identify opportunities for transformation and job creation.

Quantitative and Qualitative Analysis

The position requires strong analytical skills.

The Economist will apply quantitative and qualitative methods to economic and development questions.

This may include working with:

  • Economic datasets
  • Microdata
  • Labour market information
  • Poverty and inequality indicators
  • Productivity statistics
  • Sectoral data
  • Macroeconomic information
  • Development indicators

The objective will be to transform data and research findings into useful insights for policymakers and development practitioners.

Economic Models and Microdata

The Economist will also support the development and application of growth and inclusion models.

This includes working with microeconomic datasets and other quantitative resources to understand economic and social outcomes.

Strong data analysis capabilities will therefore be important for the successful candidate.

2. Prepare Technical Papers and Policy Briefs

Another important responsibility involves communicating economic research effectively.

The Economist will prepare materials such as:

  • Technical papers
  • Data-driven policy briefs
  • Background research notes
  • Analytical reports
  • Presentations
  • Evidence packs
  • Technical guidance materials

These documents may be used by senior economists, government officials, UNDP Country Offices and other development stakeholders.

The ability to communicate complicated economic concepts clearly will therefore be essential.

A successful candidate should be comfortable presenting technical information to both specialist and non-specialist audiences.

3. Contribute to Regional Knowledge Products

The Economist will contribute to regional knowledge products focused on economic transformation and inclusive growth.

These products can help capture research findings, policy lessons and analytical approaches that may be relevant across countries in Asia and the Pacific.

The role therefore involves not only producing analysis for individual assignments but also helping develop knowledge that can support broader regional development efforts.

Government Advisory and Country Engagement

The position also has an important government-facing component.

The Economist will support high-level policy dialogues and country-level development engagements.

4. Support High-Level Policy Dialogues

The successful candidate will provide technical inputs to policy discussions led by the IPSA-12 Senior Economist and other Inclusive Growth Team experts.

This could involve preparing:

  • Economic analysis
  • Data
  • Presentations
  • Briefing materials
  • Evidence summaries
  • Policy recommendations
  • Background research

The Economist will help ensure that policy discussions are informed by credible evidence and rigorous analysis.

5. Support UNDP Country Offices

The Economist will assist UNDP Country Offices in delivering BOLD analytical work.

This includes supporting activities such as:

  • Country capability assessments
  • Economic diagnostics
  • Growth analysis
  • Labour market assessments
  • Inclusion analysis
  • Development strategy work

The position therefore requires someone who can work effectively across teams and adapt analytical work to different country contexts.

6. Prepare Presentations and Data Visualizations

The Economist will also assist with preparing presentations, data visualizations and evidence packs for government engagements.

This means the successful candidate should not only be able to analyse data but should also be able to communicate findings visually.

The ability to convert complex economic information into clear charts, tables, presentations and concise messages can be particularly valuable in this role.

7. Participate in Missions, Consultations and Workshops

The Economist may participate in:

  • Technical missions
  • Government consultations
  • Workshops
  • Policy dialogues
  • Stakeholder meetings
  • Country-level engagements

This provides an opportunity to engage directly with policymakers, development practitioners and other stakeholders.

Programme Implementation and Coordination

Beyond research and analysis, the Economist will contribute to the planning and implementation of BOLD activities.

8. Support Planning and Delivery

The Economist will contribute to planning, monitoring and delivery of BOLD activities at both regional and country levels.

This may require coordinating different workstreams, tracking deliverables and ensuring that analytical activities are delivered according to programme objectives.

9. Support Reporting and Quality Assurance

The position will also provide analytical and reporting inputs for:

  • Donor updates
  • Internal reporting
  • Quality assurance
  • Project documentation
  • Programme monitoring

Strong organizational and communication skills will therefore complement the technical economics requirements.

10. Coordinate With Multiple Stakeholders

The Economist will coordinate with:

  • UNDP Country Offices
  • External research partners
  • Internal UNDP teams
  • Economists
  • Policy specialists
  • Government counterparts
  • Development partners

The ability to collaborate across institutions and professional disciplines is therefore important.

Knowledge Management and Learning

The role also includes responsibilities related to knowledge management.

The Economist will help ensure that analytical tools, datasets, methodologies and lessons from country-level implementation are properly maintained and documented.

11. Maintain Datasets and Analytical Tools

The successful candidate will maintain and update datasets, analytical tools and templates used across the BOLD programme.

This requires attention to detail and an understanding of data quality.

12. Capture Lessons Learned

The Economist will synthesize lessons learned from country implementation.

These lessons can then be used to improve regional guidance and strengthen future economic analysis.

13. Prepare Technical Guidance

The successful candidate may also prepare technical guidance notes covering areas such as:

  • Inclusive growth analysis
  • Job creation diagnostics
  • Economic transformation
  • Labour market analysis
  • Development strategy
  • Related economic policy topics

Reporting Structure

The Economist will report directly to the UNDP Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific Chief Economist, who also serves as the head of the Inclusive Growth Global Policy Network Team.

The successful candidate will work closely with several important stakeholders, including:

  • Inclusive Growth Team Regional Advisor
  • Economists
  • Policy specialists
  • BOLD Project Manager
  • UNDP Country Office economists
  • UNDP programme teams
  • Government counterparts
  • External partners
  • Global Policy Network colleagues
  • Other Regional Hubs where necessary

This means the position involves substantial cross-functional and international collaboration.

Competencies Required

UNDP has identified several core competencies for the position.

Achieve Results

The candidate should be able to set and align challenging but achievable objectives across multiple projects and contribute to work that creates lasting impact.

Think Innovatively

The Economist should be able to identify risks, develop new ideas and find innovative solutions to complex economic and development problems.

Learn Continuously

The role requires a willingness to continuously expand professional knowledge and diversify experience.

Adapt With Agility

The successful candidate should be comfortable managing multiple competing demands and supporting change in a complex development environment.

Act With Determination

The candidate should demonstrate initiative and remain focused on achieving results even when facing challenges or barriers.

Engage and Partner

Strong stakeholder-management skills are essential.

The Economist should be politically savvy, able to navigate complex institutional environments and capable of supporting inter-agency collaboration.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion

The candidate should appreciate the value of a diverse workforce and contribute to an inclusive working environment.

Technical Competencies

In addition to general professional competencies, the position requires technical capabilities in several areas.

Inclusive Growth and Development Planning

The candidate should understand development planning and how economic policies can contribute to inclusive growth.

Growth Strategies

Experience with economic growth strategies is relevant to the position.

Structural Transformation

The Economist should understand structural transformation and its relationship with productivity, employment and economic development.

Jobs and Livelihoods

Knowledge of labour markets, employment and job creation is important.

Poverty and Inequality Metrics

The position also requires an understanding of poverty and inequality measurement and analysis.

Data Analysis

The successful candidate should be capable of extracting, analysing and visualizing data to generate meaningful insights and support effective decision-making.

Systems Thinking

The role requires the ability to understand how different elements of an economic or development system interact.

The Economist should be able to analyse problems objectively and consider how changing one part of a system can affect other components.

Educational Requirements

Applicants must meet one of the following educational pathways.

Master’s Degree Route

An advanced university degree, such as a master’s degree or equivalent, in one of the following areas is required:

  • Economics
  • Applied Economics
  • Statistics
  • Public Policy
  • A related field

Applicants using the master’s degree pathway must also have at least 7 years of relevant professional experience.

Bachelor’s Degree Route

A first-level university degree in:

  • Economics
  • Applied Economics
  • Statistics
  • Public Policy
  • A related field

may be considered in combination with additional qualifying experience.

Under this pathway, candidates are required to have at least 9 years of relevant professional experience.

PhD

A PhD in Economics or a related discipline is considered desirable.

A doctoral degree is therefore not stated as mandatory, but it could strengthen an applicant’s profile.

Professional Experience Requirements

The vacancy requires substantial professional experience.

Candidates must have a minimum of:

  • 7 years of relevant experience with a master’s degree, or
  • 9 years of relevant experience with a bachelor’s degree.

The experience should be relevant to areas such as:

  • Applied economic analysis
  • Economic research
  • Development policy
  • Economic diagnostics
  • Labour market analysis
  • Inclusive development
  • Quantitative research
  • Economic modelling

Applicants should carefully demonstrate how their previous professional experience directly relates to these areas.

Required Professional Skills

The vacancy identifies several specific skills that applicants should possess.

Growth Diagnostics

Applicants should have experience conducting or supporting growth diagnostics.

This is particularly relevant because the BOLD programme works with governments to understand economic constraints and identify strategic development pathways.

Labour Market Analysis

Experience analysing labour markets is required.

Applicants should ideally understand employment trends, job creation, labour-force dynamics and related economic issues.

Poverty, Inequality and Inclusion Analysis

Experience with inclusion and inequality assessments is also required.

This may include working with poverty statistics, inequality indicators and other measures of socioeconomic outcomes.

Quantitative Analysis

Strong quantitative analytical capabilities are essential.

Applicants should be comfortable working with economic data and using analytical approaches to generate evidence-based insights.

Microeconomic Data

Experience working with microeconomic datasets is required or highly relevant.

Candidates should be able to work with data to investigate economic and social outcomes.

Macroeconomic Modelling

Experience with macroeconomic modelling is also identified as a required skill.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate quantitative economic expertise rather than relying solely on qualitative policy experience.

Government and Development Partner Experience

Candidates should have experience working with one or more of the following:

  • Governments
  • International organizations
  • Research institutes
  • Development partners

This requirement reflects the policy-oriented and advisory nature of the position.

Desired Skills and Experience

Some qualifications are not mandatory but are considered advantageous.

Previous UNDP or UN Experience

Previous experience working with UNDP or another UN organization is an asset.

Applicants who have already worked within the UN development system may therefore have relevant institutional experience.

Knowledge of Asia and the Pacific

Familiarity with development challenges and policy contexts across Asia and the Pacific is highly desirable.

This is particularly relevant because the role is located within UNDP’s Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific and involves supporting countries across the region.

Technical Guidance Experience

Experience preparing technical guidance notes on subjects such as inclusive growth analysis and job creation diagnostics is also desirable.

Language Requirement

Fluency in English is required.

Applicants should therefore be able to communicate effectively in written and spoken English, particularly because the position involves preparing technical documents, participating in policy discussions and engaging with international stakeholders.

Who Should Apply?

This position is most appropriate for experienced economists and development professionals who have a strong combination of technical economic expertise, quantitative analysis skills and development policy experience.

Potentially suitable professional profiles include:

  • Economists
  • Development economists
  • Applied economists
  • Economic policy specialists
  • Economic researchers
  • Labour market specialists
  • Inclusive growth specialists
  • Public policy professionals with strong economics experience
  • Quantitative development researchers
  • Economic analysts
  • Professionals working on poverty and inequality
  • Development strategy specialists

However, meeting a professional profile alone is not enough. Candidates must also satisfy the vacancy’s Tier 0, Tier 1 or Tier 2 eligibility requirements.

Understanding the UNDP Tiered Application System

One of the most important aspects of this vacancy is its tiered application process.

The vacancy is specifically advertised as:

“Economist – Development Strategy [Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants]”

Applicants should therefore determine whether they fall within one of these categories before investing time in the application.

Tier 0

Tier 0 includes UNDP, UNCDF and UNV international personnel holding permanent or fixed-term appointments whose posts will be abolished, or whose contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Tier 1

Tier 1 includes other UNDP, UNCDF and UNV staff members holding permanent or fixed-term appointments.

Tier 2

Tier 2 includes:

  • UNDP/UNCDF/UNV personnel holding temporary appointments
  • Personnel on regular PSA contracts
  • Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

Tier 3 and Other Candidates

The vacancy description explains that Tier 3, or vacancies without a tier indication, generally cover other contract types and external candidates.

However, this particular vacancy explicitly states Tier 0, Tier 1 and Tier 2.

Therefore, external applicants who do not fall into one of these categories should not assume that they are eligible simply because they meet the educational and professional requirements.

Nationality, Race and Geographic Eligibility

The vacancy does not specify a particular race, ethnicity or nationality as an eligibility requirement.

UNDP states that it is an equal opportunity employer and encourages qualified applicants from diverse backgrounds.

However, this should not be confused with the tier eligibility requirement.

For this specific vacancy, eligibility is primarily determined by:

  1. The applicant’s UNDP/UNCDF/UNV personnel status and applicable tier;
  2. Educational qualifications;
  3. Relevant professional experience;
  4. Required technical skills;
  5. English language proficiency;
  6. Other requirements specified in the vacancy.

The job is based in Bangkok, Thailand, and familiarity with Asia and the Pacific is desirable.

Important Deadline

The application deadline is:

9 September 2026 at 3:59 AM

APPLY HERE

For more information visit the UNDP website HERE

Because the deadline is stated in the vacancy system, applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications.

Candidates should also check the official recruitment platform for any changes to the vacancy or application timeline before submitting.

For more global opportunities visit OFY Website HERE

Contract and Working Arrangement

The position is offered under an International Personnel Service Agreement (IPSA).

Key contract details include:

  • Grade: IPSA-11
  • Duration: 1 year
  • Schedule: Full time
  • Duty Station: Bangkok, Thailand

The position sits within UNDP’s Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific and is connected to the organization’s Inclusive Growth practice area.

Why This Opportunity Is Significant

This opportunity could be particularly valuable for an eligible professional interested in the intersection of economics, public policy and international development.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to work on issues that directly affect economic development strategies, including:

  • Inclusive economic growth
  • Employment
  • Productivity
  • Labour markets
  • Inequality
  • Poverty
  • Structural transformation
  • Development planning
  • Government policy
  • Economic reform
  • Sustainable development

The position also provides exposure to high-level government advisory work and regional development initiatives.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Eligible candidates should tailor their application carefully to the vacancy.

1. Demonstrate Relevant Economic Experience

Do not simply list previous positions.

Explain how your professional experience involved:

  • Economic analysis
  • Research
  • Development policy
  • Labour markets
  • Growth diagnostics
  • Inequality
  • Productivity
  • Structural transformation

2. Highlight Quantitative Skills

Applicants should clearly demonstrate their experience with:

  • Data analysis
  • Microdata
  • Economic modelling
  • Macroeconomic analysis
  • Statistical analysis
  • Data visualization

Where possible, explain the outcomes produced through your analysis.

3. Demonstrate Government or Development Experience

If you have worked with governments, UN organizations, development agencies, research institutions or development partners, make this highly visible in your application.

4. Show Policy Impact

UNDP is not simply looking for someone who can analyse data.

The position involves turning evidence into development strategies and policy advice.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate how their previous research or analysis contributed to:

  • Policy decisions
  • Development programmes
  • Government strategies
  • Institutional reforms
  • Economic planning
  • Programme implementation

5. Highlight Stakeholder Engagement

Mention experience working with:

  • Senior officials
  • Government representatives
  • International organizations
  • Development partners
  • Researchers
  • Multilateral institutions
  • Cross-functional teams

6. Tailor Your Application to BOLD

Because BOLD is central to the position, applicants should demonstrate experience that connects economic research with practical development strategy.

Show that you understand how diagnostics can lead to strategic policy recommendations and reform pathways.

What Makes a Strong Candidate?

A particularly strong candidate would likely combine several of the following characteristics:

  • Advanced economics or related academic training
  • Extensive professional experience
  • Strong quantitative analysis skills
  • Experience with economic research
  • Labour market expertise
  • Growth diagnostics experience
  • Understanding of inequality and poverty
  • Experience with development policy
  • Knowledge of structural transformation
  • Experience working with governments
  • International development experience
  • Strong writing and presentation skills
  • Data visualization capabilities
  • Stakeholder-management skills
  • Experience working across countries or institutions
  • Strong English communication skills
  • Understanding of development challenges in Asia and the Pacific

Equal Opportunity Commitment

UNDP states that it is committed to equal opportunity and values diversity as an expression of the many nations and cultures in which it operates.

The organization’s employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role and are made without discrimination.

UNDP also emphasizes its commitment to an inclusive workplace where personnel can contribute, develop professionally and access career opportunities.

Harassment, Exploitation and Abuse

UNDP states that it does not tolerate:

  • Harassment
  • Sexual harassment
  • Exploitation
  • Discrimination
  • Abuse of authority

Selected candidates are subject to relevant checks and are expected to follow applicable UNDP standards and principles.

UNDP Scam Alert

Applicants should be careful about fraudulent recruitment schemes.

UNDP states that it does not charge a fee at any stage of the recruitment process.

Candidates should therefore be extremely cautious if anyone claiming to represent UNDP requests payment for:

  • Application processing
  • Recruitment
  • Interviews
  • Visa arrangements
  • Employment
  • Training
  • Document verification

Applicants should rely on official UNDP recruitment channels for legitimate information.

UNDP May Select Multiple Candidates

The vacancy notice states that UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from the announcement.

The organization may also retain applications and consider candidates who apply for this position for other similar positions at the same grade level with similar job descriptions, experience and educational requirements.

This means that an application could potentially be relevant to similar opportunities within UNDP where the candidate meets the requirements.

Use of AI During the Application Process

The vacancy also draws attention to UNDP’s guidance for candidates regarding the responsible use of artificial intelligence in recruitment and selection.

Applicants who use AI tools when preparing application materials should therefore ensure that their submissions accurately represent their own qualifications, experience and professional capabilities.

Candidates should avoid submitting generic or fabricated information.

Every statement in an application should be truthful and defensible during the recruitment process.

Key Facts at a Glance

Category Details
Organization United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
Position Economist – Development Strategy
Job ID 36454
Location Bangkok, Thailand
Grade IPSA-11
Contract International Personnel Service Agreement
Duration 1 year
Schedule Full time
Practice Area Inclusive Growth
Bureau Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific
Education Master’s + 7 years OR Bachelor’s + 9 years
Preferred Doctorate PhD in Economics or related field
Language English
Experience Applied economic analysis, research or development policy
Deadline 9 September 2026, 3:59 AM
Eligible Tiers Tier 0, Tier 1 and Tier 2

Final Thoughts

The UNDP Economist – Development Strategy position represents a significant opportunity for an experienced economics and development professional interested in contributing to high-level development strategy and inclusive growth initiatives.

The role goes far beyond traditional economic research. It combines economic analysis, data, development policy, government advisory, labour market research, growth diagnostics, programme coordination and knowledge management.

The successful candidate will contribute to the BOLD initiative and support UNDP’s efforts to help governments transform economic evidence into practical development strategies.

However, one of the most important points for potential applicants is the tier restriction. This vacancy is specifically advertised for Tier 0, Tier 1 and Tier 2 applicants, meaning candidates must carefully verify that they fall within the applicable UNDP, UNCDF or UNV personnel categories before applying.

For those who meet the tier requirements and possess the required academic background, substantial relevant experience and technical economic skills, this role offers an opportunity to work at the intersection of economics, public policy and international development from UNDP’s regional hub in Bangkok.

Eligible candidates should prepare their applications carefully, demonstrate clear evidence of their economic and development expertise, and submit their applications before the 9 September 2026 deadline at 3:59 AM.

Most importantly, applicants should ensure that every qualification and professional achievement presented in their application is accurate, relevant and clearly connected to the responsibilities of the Economist – Development Strategy position.

item.content:encoded:
The Management Intern, Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Arizona State University (ASU) is an exciting professional opportunity for individuals interested in higher education administration, scholarship program management, student services, project coordination, and global education initiatives.

Based at Arizona State University’s Tempe campus in Arizona, USA, this part-time position offers a salary of $21 per hour and provides hands-on experience supporting the administration and delivery of the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program. The role is particularly relevant for candidates with strong organizational, communication, administrative, customer service, and project coordination skills.

The position supports a program designed to provide comprehensive scholarships and holistic support to young people from across the African continent who are committed to giving back to their communities.

Applications are currently open, and interested candidates should submit their application before the stated deadline.

Opportunity Overview

  • Position: Management Intern, Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program
  • Institution: Arizona State University (ASU)
  • Department: Office of Global Academic Initiatives
  • Job Family: Administrative Support
  • Job Profile: Administrative Support Assistant 1, Non-Exempt
  • Opportunity Type: Part-time employment/internship
  • Location: Tempe Campus, Arizona, USA
  • Work Type: Part-time
  • Salary: $21 per hour
  • Driving Required: No
  • Application Deadline: September 4, 2026
  • Application Time: Before 11:59 PM Arizona time the day before the posted end date
  • Job Requisition ID: JR125901

About the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at ASU

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Arizona State University is designed to provide comprehensive scholarships and holistic support to talented young people from across Africa.

The program goes beyond financial assistance by supporting scholars throughout their educational journey and helping them develop the knowledge, skills, leadership capabilities, and networks needed to contribute to their communities.

The Management Intern will become part of the administrative and operational team supporting this important initiative.

This makes the position particularly valuable for someone who wants to build experience at the intersection of:

  • Higher education
  • International development
  • Scholarship administration
  • Student support
  • Program management
  • Project coordination
  • Global education
  • Administrative operations
  • Communications
  • Event coordination

What Does the Management Intern Do?

The Management Intern will provide administrative, coordination, and programmatic support to the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program team.

The position involves supporting the program’s day-to-day activities while also contributing to application and selection processes, scholar programming, communications, special projects, and operational improvements.

The successful candidate will work under the administrative direction of the Assistant Director and collaborate with other members of the Scholars Program team.

The role therefore combines administrative support, project coordination, communication, applicant support, event planning, and program operations.

1. Support Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program Operations

One of the major responsibilities of the intern will be supporting the overall administration and coordination of the Scholars Program.

This can involve helping the team with:

  • Program activities
  • Administrative tasks
  • Projects
  • Communications
  • Operational processes
  • Documentation
  • Coordination activities
  • Day-to-day program needs

The intern will help ensure that assigned activities are completed efficiently and that the program team has the administrative support required to deliver its work effectively.

This responsibility can provide valuable exposure to how a large international education initiative operates within a major American university.

2. Support the Scholarship Application and Selection Process

A significant component of this position involves supporting the scholarship application cycle.

The intern will assist with administrative activities connected to applications and candidate selection.

Responsibilities may include:

Application Launch Support

The intern may assist the Scholars Program team when applications are launched, helping ensure that administrative processes and applicant communications are properly coordinated.

Applicant Tracking

The position involves helping maintain accurate applicant information and tracking application-related activities.

Strong attention to detail will therefore be important.

Responding to Applicant Inquiries

The intern will help respond to applicant questions through Salesforce.

This means candidates should be comfortable communicating professionally with applicants and handling questions in a responsive and organized manner.

Interview Scheduling

The intern will assist with scheduling interviews as part of the selection process.

This requires effective calendar management, communication, organization, and attention to deadlines.

Applicant Communications

The intern will also support communications with applicants throughout the selection process.

This could involve sending or coordinating relevant information, responding to questions, and supporting follow-up activities.

Administrative Follow-Up

Additional administrative tasks associated with applications and selection may also be assigned.

This makes organizational skills particularly important because the intern may need to keep track of multiple candidates, deadlines, communications, and processes simultaneously.

3. Support Scholar Programming and Events

The role is not limited to administrative work.

The Management Intern will also contribute to the planning and delivery of activities and initiatives for Scholars.

This may include supporting:

  • Scholar events
  • Educational programming
  • In-person activities
  • Virtual activities
  • Program initiatives
  • Workshops
  • Communications materials
  • Participant engagement activities

The intern may also assist with developing program content and materials.

In some situations, the intern may support or co-facilitate activities conducted either virtually or in person.

This can provide useful experience for candidates interested in event management, program management, stakeholder engagement, training, facilitation, and communications.

4. Collect and Organize Participant Feedback

Another responsibility involves collecting and organizing feedback from participants.

Participant feedback can help the Scholars Program understand what is working effectively and where future programming can be improved.

The intern may therefore help:

  1. Collect participant feedback.
  2. Organize feedback and related information.
  3. Maintain accurate records.
  4. Support the team in reviewing participant responses.
  5. Help inform future program activities.

This responsibility highlights the importance of data organization, communication, documentation, and analytical thinking.

5. Support Special Projects and Process Improvements

The Management Intern will also collaborate with Scholars Program staff on special projects.

These projects may arise based on the program’s changing priorities and operational requirements.

The intern may provide support with:

  • Project activities
  • Deliverables
  • Process improvements
  • Administrative coordination
  • Program initiatives
  • Emerging priorities
  • Operational projects

This aspect of the role could be particularly valuable for candidates interested in project management and program management because it provides exposure to real-world project coordination within a global education program.

6. Provide Additional Administrative and Programmatic Support

The successful candidate should be prepared to perform other duties assigned by the Scholars Program team.

These responsibilities will be aligned with the needs and priorities of the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program.

Because program priorities can change, the ideal candidate should be adaptable and comfortable working in an environment where responsibilities may evolve.

Salary and Working Arrangement

The position offers a stated salary of:

$21 per hour

The position is classified as part-time.

The job is based at Arizona State University’s Tempe campus.

The working environment is primarily a regular, climate-controlled office setting, with an expectation of regular in-person work.

The intern will also support both in-person and virtual activities, meetings, and events.

Some schedule flexibility may occasionally be required depending on program activities and events.

Working Environment and Physical Requirements

The position involves regular use of a:

  • Desktop computer
  • Laptop computer
  • Virtual communication platforms
  • Collaboration tools

The position may also require extended periods of sitting.

Occasional physical activities may include:

  • Bending
  • Stooping
  • Reaching
  • Lifting materials weighing up to 20 pounds

Applicants should consider these working conditions when evaluating whether the position is suitable for them.

Minimum Qualifications

Arizona State University states that applicants must meet the minimum qualification of:

A high school diploma; OR any equivalent combination of experience and/or training from which comparable knowledge, skills, and abilities have been achieved.

This means that the position does not require a specific university degree as a minimum qualification.

However, applicants should carefully demonstrate relevant experience and skills in their resume because the university also wants applications to clearly demonstrate how candidates meet the desired qualifications.

Desired Qualifications

Although the minimum qualification is relatively accessible, ASU has identified several preferred qualifications that can strengthen an applicant’s candidacy.

1. Familiarity With the Mastercard Foundation

Experience or familiarity with the Mastercard Foundation and its education-related contexts is desirable.

Candidates who understand the Foundation’s work and the broader objectives of education access and development in Africa may be able to demonstrate stronger alignment with the position.

2. Customer Service Experience

Experience with customer service standards, methods, and practices is desirable.

This is particularly relevant because the intern may communicate directly with scholarship applicants and other stakeholders.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate their ability to:

  • Respond professionally
  • Communicate clearly
  • Handle questions
  • Provide timely assistance
  • Maintain professionalism
  • Work effectively with different audiences

3. Program Coordination and Project Management

Working knowledge of basic program coordination and project management principles is another desired qualification.

This is an important aspect of the position for individuals pursuing careers in project management.

Experience coordinating activities, tracking deliverables, organizing events, managing timelines, or supporting projects can therefore be relevant.

4. Strong Organizational Skills

The successful candidate should be highly organized.

ASU specifically highlights the ability to:

  • Maintain accurate records
  • Manage multiple priorities
  • Complete assigned activities within established timelines

Applicants should make these capabilities visible in their resumes rather than simply listing “organized” as a skill.

For example, previous administrative, executive assistant, project coordination, event management, or program support responsibilities can help demonstrate this competency.

5. Effective Communication Skills

Strong communication skills are essential.

The intern will communicate with applicants, students, staff, faculty, and other stakeholders.

The successful candidate should therefore be capable of providing:

  • Responsive communication
  • Professional communication
  • Clear information
  • Appropriate follow-up
  • Effective stakeholder engagement

Both written and interpersonal communication skills can be valuable for this role.

6. Google Workspace Skills

Applicants should have proficiency with Google Workspace applications.

The position specifically identifies:

  • Google Docs
  • Google Sheets
  • Google Forms
  • Google Drive

These tools may be used for:

  • Communication
  • Applicant tracking
  • Documentation
  • Data organization
  • Program operations
  • Collaboration
  • Information management

Candidates should consider including specific examples of how they have used these applications in previous roles.

7. Relationship-Building Skills

The position requires the ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with:

  • Students
  • Staff
  • Faculty
  • Program stakeholders
  • Applicants
  • Other members of the university community

Strong interpersonal skills will therefore be important.

8. Judgment, Discretion and Adaptability

The intern may encounter confidential or sensitive information during the application and selection process.

ASU therefore seeks candidates who demonstrate:

  • Sound judgment
  • Discretion
  • Confidentiality
  • Adaptability
  • Collaboration
  • Independence
  • Responsibility

The successful applicant should be able to complete assigned responsibilities independently while knowing when appropriate guidance is needed.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity may be particularly suitable for individuals seeking professional experience in:

  • Administrative support
  • Executive assistance
  • Higher education administration
  • Scholarship administration
  • Program coordination
  • Project management
  • Student services
  • International education
  • Nonprofit program management
  • Global development
  • Event management
  • Communications
  • Customer service
  • Applicant support

Candidates with previous experience in administrative or coordination roles may find their background particularly relevant.

Why This Opportunity Is Valuable

The Management Intern position provides more than an hourly job.

It offers an opportunity to gain practical experience supporting a major international scholarship initiative within one of the United States’ prominent public universities.

Some of the potential professional benefits include:

Practical Program Management Experience

You can gain exposure to real-world program coordination and project activities.

Scholarship Administration Experience

The role provides direct exposure to application, applicant communication, tracking, interviews, and selection-related administration.

Higher Education Experience

Working within Arizona State University can provide valuable insight into university operations and global academic initiatives.

International Education Exposure

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program focuses on young people from across Africa, giving the position an international and cross-cultural dimension.

Professional Communication

The position involves communication with applicants, students, staff, faculty, and other stakeholders.

Event and Program Experience

The intern will help support scholar programming, events, activities, and initiatives.

Technology Experience

The position provides opportunities to use tools such as Google Workspace and Salesforce.

Project Management Exposure

Candidates interested in becoming project managers can gain practical experience with projects, deliverables, coordination, timelines, and process improvements.

About the Office of Global Academic Initiatives

The position is located within the Office of Global Academic Initiatives.

The office works to build global capacity and global agility across the university.

It serves as a central coordinating unit for strategic university partnerships and focuses on increasing access to quality education globally.

This makes the position especially relevant to candidates interested in international education, global partnerships, academic programs, and international development.

Is Driving Required?

No.

The job posting explicitly states that driving is not required for this position.

Application Requirements

Applicants must submit the required application materials electronically.

ASU requires:

  1. Cover letter
  2. Resume or CV

Applicants can upload the documents separately or combine all required materials into one PDF.

If combining the documents, applicants should make sure the file is clearly labeled and includes their name.

Important Resume Instructions

ASU provides specific instructions for resumes submitted for this position.

Your resume should include employment information in month and year format.

For example:

6/04 to 8/14

For every position, applicants should clearly provide:

  • Job title
  • Employer name
  • Employment dates
  • Job duties

Your resume should demonstrate how your experience and background meet both the minimum and desired qualifications.

This is particularly important because simply listing previous job titles may not adequately demonstrate your suitability for the role.

How to Strengthen Your Resume

Because this position emphasizes administration, coordination, communication, and project support, applicants should tailor their resumes accordingly.

Where applicable, highlight experience involving:

  • Calendar management
  • Applicant or client communication
  • Data entry and tracking
  • Google Workspace
  • Salesforce or CRM systems
  • Event coordination
  • Project coordination
  • Scheduling
  • Record management
  • Stakeholder communication
  • Administrative support
  • Confidential information
  • Reporting
  • Process improvement
  • Team collaboration

Use specific accomplishments whenever possible.

For example, instead of simply writing:

“Provided administrative support.”

A stronger resume statement could explain what you supported, who you supported, and the result of your work.

Important Application Warning

ASU provides an important warning to applicants:

Do not withdraw your application simply to make edits.

According to the university, once an application is withdrawn, it cannot be edited, reactivated, or replaced with a new submission.

If you have questions or need assistance with the application, ASU recommends contacting the Office of Human Resources Talent Acquisition before the posting closes.

Experience Equivalency for Part-Time Positions

ASU also provides information about experience equivalency.

Graduate Assistant, Intern, and part-time positions are counted as half time for experience equivalency.

According to the posting:

One year equals six months of experience.

Applicants should keep this policy in mind when evaluating how their experience may be assessed.

Background and Employment Verification

Applicants should ensure that all information submitted is accurate and complete.

Arizona State University conducts pre-employment screening that may include verification of:

  • Work history
  • Academic credentials
  • Licenses
  • Certifications

Employment is contingent upon successfully passing the required background check.

The university also states that a criminal background check is conducted for all positions.

A fingerprint check is not required for this particular position.

Important Deadline

The application deadline is:

September 4, 2026

The position specifies that applications should be submitted before 11:59 PM Arizona time the day before the posted end date.

Because deadlines can be affected by time-zone differences, applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their materials.

Applicants should ideally complete and submit their application well before the deadline.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should apply through Arizona State University’s official careers system.

Application page: APPLY HERE

Arizona State University’s website: HERE

Applicants should prepare their cover letter and tailored resume/CV before beginning the application.

External applicants should create an external candidate account using a personal, non-ASU email address and proceed through the external application process.

Category of the Opportunity

Category: Job / Part-Time Internship

This is a paid, part-time Management Intern position at Arizona State University.

Who Qualifies for This Opportunity?

The minimum stated qualification is:

  • A high school diploma, OR
  • An equivalent combination of experience and/or training that provides comparable knowledge, skills, and abilities.

The university also identifies several desired qualifications, including program/project coordination knowledge, customer service experience, strong organizational and communication skills, Google Workspace proficiency, relationship-building abilities, and sound judgment when handling sensitive information.

Geographic and Continental Eligibility

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program itself supports young people from across the African continent. However, this specific job posting is for an employment position based at Arizona State University’s Tempe campus in the United States.

The job posting does not state a race-specific restriction or say that only African applicants may apply for this particular employment position. Therefore, applicants should not assume that the job is legally restricted only to a particular race or nationality based solely on the program’s target population.

Candidates should review the official ASU application requirements and employment eligibility requirements before applying.

Conclusion

The Management Intern, Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Arizona State University is a strong opportunity for someone looking to develop practical experience in administration, higher education, scholarship program operations, project coordination, student engagement, and international education.

The position combines administrative responsibilities with meaningful exposure to the management of a major scholarship initiative serving young people from across Africa.

With a salary of $21 per hour, part-time employment, exposure to application and selection processes, event and scholar programming, project support, stakeholder communication, and process improvement, the role can provide useful professional experience for individuals building careers in project management, program management, higher education administration, international development, and administrative leadership.

Applicants should pay particular attention to the resume requirements, demonstrate their relevant experience clearly, prepare a strong cover letter, and submit all required materials before the deadline.

For candidates whose experience aligns with administration, coordination, communication, project support, and global education, this is an opportunity worth considering and applying for well before the deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Maryland Do Good Accelerator Fellows Program is an opportunity for current University of Maryland, College Park students who are developing projects, social ventures, or initiatives designed to create meaningful change in society, the environment, or the future.

Organized by the Do Good Institute at the University of Maryland, the Accelerator Fellows Program is designed to give students the practical support, mentorship, resources, workspace, and time they need to move promising ideas forward and increase their social impact.

For students who are already implementing a project and want to strengthen, test, develop, or scale their work, the program provides an opportunity to spend a semester working within a supportive environment alongside coaches and other students pursuing social impact.

The Fall 2026 Accelerator Fellows Program will run for eight weeks, from September 28 through November 20, 2026. Selected fellows are required to dedicate 8 hours per week to the Do Good Accelerator and will receive a $2,000 stipend upon successful completion of the fellowship.

Applications open on August 3, 2026, and close on September 14, 2026.

About the University of Maryland Do Good Accelerator Fellows Program

The Do Good Accelerator Fellows Program is a student-focused initiative created to help University of Maryland students turn ideas and social impact projects into stronger, more sustainable initiatives.

The program recognizes that having a good idea is only the beginning. Students working on social ventures often need access to experienced guidance, resources, a dedicated workspace, development opportunities, and a community of people who understand the challenges involved in creating impact.

The Accelerator provides these forms of support through an intensive eight-week program.

Participants can use the fellowship to:

  • Explore and develop an existing project.
  • Test an idea or approach.
  • Improve a project that is already operating.
  • Strengthen the impact of a social venture.
  • Develop strategies for scaling an initiative.
  • Receive individualized coaching.
  • Learn practical skills through workshops and webinars.
  • Connect with other students working on meaningful projects.
  • Access resources and workspace.
  • Dedicate structured time to advancing their initiative.

The program is particularly suited to students who have moved beyond the initial idea stage and are already implementing their projects.

Fall 2026 Accelerator Fellows Program

The Fall 2026 cohort is an eight-week fellowship program designed for current University of Maryland, College Park students.

Unlike opportunities that focus primarily on developing an idea from scratch, the Accelerator specifically identifies the ideal fellow as someone who is already in the implementation phase and is currently making an impact within the community.

This means applicants should ideally have more than just an idea. They should be able to demonstrate that they are actively working on a project, initiative, organization, social venture, or other form of impact-driven work.

The program can then provide the support needed to help the student take that work to the next level.

Fall 2026 Program Dates and Timeline

Applicants should keep the following dates in mind:

  • Application Opens: August 3, 2026
  • Application Closes: September 14, 2026
  • Fall Fellows Notified: September 24, 2026
  • Program Begins: September 28, 2026
  • Program Ends: November 20, 2026
  • Program Duration: 8 weeks

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the University of Maryland Do Good Accelerator Fellows Program Fall 2026 cohort is September 14, 2026.

Students interested in the opportunity should complete their applications and submit all required information before the deadline.

Applicants are encouraged not to wait until the final day to apply, particularly if additional information or preparation is required for the application.

What Does the Do Good Accelerator Fellows Program Offer?

The University of Maryland Do Good Accelerator provides several forms of support intended to help fellows strengthen their projects and increase their impact.

1. One-on-One Coaching and Advising

One of the central features of the fellowship is individualized coaching.

Each week, fellows participate in one-on-one coaching sessions designed to address the specific needs of their projects.

This is particularly valuable because social impact initiatives can face very different challenges depending on their stage of development.

Through coaching, students can receive guidance as they work through issues related to developing, testing, improving, or scaling their projects.

The individualized nature of the coaching also allows fellows to focus on the areas where their particular initiative needs the most attention.

2. Workshops and Webinars

Fellows will participate in developmental activities designed to expose them to useful tools, knowledge, and resources.

The program includes:

  • Workshops
  • Webinars
  • Panel discussions
  • Community events
  • Other developmental programming

These activities are intended to help students develop diverse skills that can contribute to the success of their projects.

Rather than simply receiving theoretical information, fellows can use what they learn to address practical challenges within their initiatives.

3. Dedicated Workspace and Resources

The program provides fellows with access to workspace and resources through the Do Good Accelerator.

Having a dedicated environment can be particularly useful for students balancing academic responsibilities with project development.

The fellowship creates structured time for students to focus on their initiatives and work alongside other students who are also pursuing social impact.

4. Community of Like-Minded Students

Another important component of the program is the opportunity to become part of a community of students working on projects intended to create positive change.

Fellows participate in group activities and community programming where they can interact with peers who are also developing their own initiatives.

This environment can encourage:

  • Collaboration
  • Knowledge sharing
  • Peer learning
  • Networking
  • Exposure to different approaches to social impact
  • New ideas and perspectives

Being surrounded by other students who are actively working on meaningful projects can also help participants remain motivated throughout the fellowship.

$2,000 Stipend for Successful Fellows

Selected Fall 2026 fellows will receive a $2,000 stipend upon successful completion of the fellowship.

This is an important financial benefit for students because the program requires fellows to dedicate 8 hours each week to the Do Good Accelerator.

The stipend is therefore tied to successful completion of the fellowship rather than simply being an upfront award.

Applicants should understand the program’s participation requirements before applying and be prepared to commit the required time throughout the eight-week program.

Weekly Time Commitment

Fall 2026 fellows are required to work 8 hours per week at the Do Good Accelerator.

During those weekly hours, students will participate in activities including:

  1. One-on-one coaching sessions.
  2. Independent work on their projects.
  3. Workshops and webinars.
  4. Panel discussions.
  5. Community activities.
  6. Other developmental programming.

This structure is intended to balance focused independent project work with mentorship and collaborative learning.

Students considering applying should evaluate their academic schedules and other commitments to make sure they can consistently dedicate eight hours each week to the program.

Who Should Apply?

The Accelerator Fellows Program is particularly relevant for students who are already actively working on an initiative.

The University of Maryland identifies the ideal student as someone who is in the implementation phase and is currently impacting the community.

A strong prospective applicant could therefore be someone who:

  • Has an established social impact project.
  • Is actively implementing an initiative.
  • Has already begun creating community impact.
  • Is developing a social venture.
  • Wants to test or improve an existing approach.
  • Wants to scale an existing project.
  • Needs professional coaching and guidance.
  • Would benefit from structured development time.
  • Wants access to workshops and useful resources.
  • Is interested in learning alongside other student changemakers.

Simply having an idea may not make someone the strongest candidate because the program specifically emphasizes students who are already implementing their work.

What Types of Projects Can Benefit From the Program?

The information provided does not restrict the Accelerator to one particular social impact sector.

The program broadly refers to ideas and projects that could change:

  • Someone’s life
  • The environment
  • The future

This creates room for students working on different types of social impact initiatives.

Potential examples could include projects addressing:

  • Community development
  • Education
  • Environmental sustainability
  • Social entrepreneurship
  • Public service
  • Nonprofit initiatives
  • Community empowerment
  • Other social or environmental challenges

However, applicants should focus on accurately describing their actual project rather than attempting to reshape their initiative simply to fit a perceived category.

The strongest applications are likely to clearly explain the problem being addressed, what the project is doing, the impact already achieved, and what additional support is needed to move the initiative forward.

Eligibility Requirements

The Fall 2026 Accelerator Fellows Program is open to all current University of Maryland, College Park students.

This is the primary eligibility requirement explicitly stated in the program information.

Applicants should be:

  • Current students at the University of Maryland, College Park.
  • Working on a project, initiative, or social venture that can benefit from the Accelerator’s support.
  • Ideally, in the implementation phase of their project and already creating community impact.
  • Able to commit 8 hours per week during the fellowship.
  • Able to participate in the program from September 28 to November 20, 2026.

Academic Major Requirements

The announcement does not state that applicants must study a particular subject.

Therefore, no specific major or field of study should be assumed to be required based on the available program information.

GPA Requirement

No minimum GPA requirement is stated in the provided announcement.

Students should nevertheless carefully review the official application portal for any additional requirements or questions that may apply during the application process.

Age Requirement

No specific age requirement is stated in the program information provided.

Nationality and Geographic Eligibility

The announcement does not identify a nationality requirement or restriction.

However, the program is specifically open to current University of Maryland, College Park students.

Consequently, this should not be treated as a general fellowship open to anyone around the world.

International students who are currently enrolled at the University of Maryland, College Park may potentially qualify because eligibility is based on current student status rather than a stated nationality or continental restriction.

Someone who is not currently enrolled at UMD College Park would not qualify based on the eligibility criteria provided.

Race and Ethnicity Requirements

The provided program information does not specify any race, ethnicity, or racial eligibility requirement.

The opportunity is described as being open to all current University of Maryland, College Park students.

Program Benefits at a Glance

Successful fellows can benefit from:

  • $2,000 stipend upon successful completion.
  • Eight-week structured fellowship experience.
  • One-on-one coaching and advising.
  • Workshops and webinars.
  • Panel discussions and community events.
  • Access to workspace.
  • Dedicated time to work on a project.
  • Developmental activities and resources.
  • Networking with like-minded student innovators.
  • Opportunities to strengthen an existing social impact initiative.
  • Support for exploring, testing, or scaling a project or social venture.

How to Apply for the University of Maryland Accelerator Fellows Program

Students interested in the Fall 2026 Accelerator Fellows Program can submit their applications through the official University of Maryland Do Good Accelerator application portal.

Application Portal:

https://webportalapp.com/sp/login/acceleratorfellows

Official Do Good Institute Website: https://dogood.umd.edu/research-impact/projects/accelerator-fellows

More fellowship opportunities visit the OFY Website HERE

 

Applicants should review the application requirements carefully and provide information that clearly demonstrates their project’s current stage and impact.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Although the announcement does not provide a detailed scoring rubric, applicants can strengthen their applications by clearly communicating the substance and progress of their work.

1. Explain the Problem

Start by clearly explaining the problem your initiative is addressing.

A strong description should make it easy for someone unfamiliar with your project to understand:

  • What problem exists?
  • Who is affected?
  • Why does the problem matter?
  • Why does it need attention?

2. Demonstrate That You Are Already Taking Action

Because the ideal Accelerator Fellow is in the implementation phase, applicants should clearly distinguish between an idea and an active project.

If applicable, describe:

  • What you have already done.
  • Who has benefited.
  • Where the project is being implemented.
  • How long the initiative has been operating.
  • What results you have achieved.
  • Evidence of community engagement.

Concrete examples can make the project’s progress easier to understand.

3. Explain Your Impact

Don’t simply state that your project is creating impact.

Explain what that impact looks like.

For example, applicants might discuss measurable outcomes such as:

  • Number of people reached.
  • Number of beneficiaries served.
  • Communities involved.
  • Partnerships established.
  • Services delivered.
  • Environmental outcomes.
  • Educational outcomes.
  • Revenue or sustainability progress for a social venture.

The specific measurements will depend on the nature of the project.

4. Identify Your Biggest Challenges

The Accelerator exists to provide support, so applicants should be honest about the areas where their projects need development.

Consider explaining challenges involving:

  • Strategy.
  • Scaling.
  • Sustainability.
  • Operations.
  • Community engagement.
  • Partnerships.
  • Measuring impact.
  • Project development.
  • Resource mobilization.
  • Communication.

This can help demonstrate why participating in the Accelerator would be valuable to the project.

5. Explain How the Accelerator Can Help

Applicants should connect their project’s needs with the resources available through the program.

For example, you could explain how you would benefit from:

  • One-on-one coaching.
  • Workshops.
  • Expert guidance.
  • Peer learning.
  • Workspace.
  • Dedicated project-development time.
  • Community connections.
  • Developmental programming.

The goal is to show that you understand what the Accelerator provides and have a clear reason for wanting to participate.

Why the University of Maryland Accelerator Fellowship Stands Out

The Accelerator Fellows Program is different from a conventional scholarship because its primary purpose is not simply to provide financial assistance for education.

It is designed around project development and social impact.

The $2,000 stipend is one component of the program, but fellows also receive structured coaching, developmental programming, resources, workspace, and a community of peers.

For a student who already has a project making an impact, this combination can provide both the time and support needed to strengthen the initiative.

The program can also give students an opportunity to develop practical skills beyond what they may learn through their academic coursework.

What Happens During the Eight-Week Fellowship?

The program combines several activities rather than requiring students to spend all eight hours each week in workshops.

Fellows will spend time working independently on their projects, receiving coaching, participating in developmental activities, and engaging with other students.

Independent Project Work

Students will dedicate structured time to advancing their individual projects.

This could involve developing strategies, testing ideas, improving operations, working with beneficiaries, measuring impact, building partnerships, or addressing other project-specific needs.

Coaching Sessions

Participants will engage in one-on-one sessions designed to provide personalized guidance based on the needs of their individual projects.

Developmental Programming

Workshops, webinars, panel discussions, and community events will expose fellows to tools and resources that can support their development.

Peer and Community Engagement

Group activities provide opportunities to interact with other students pursuing social impact and learn from their experiences.

This combination creates a structured environment in which students can both work on their projects and learn how to improve them.

Questions About the Program

Students who have questions about the Accelerator Fellows Program can contact Kisha McNeill, Do Good Accelerator Manager.

Email: kisham@umd.edu

Kisha McNeill serves as Manager of the Do Good Accelerator at the University of Maryland Do Good Institute.

Applicants with questions about eligibility, the application process, or the fellowship structure can contact the program manager for clarification.

Important Things Applicants Should Know

Before applying, prospective fellows should keep several points in mind.

The Opportunity Is University-Specific

This is not a fellowship that is open to the general public. Applicants must be current University of Maryland, College Park students.

The Program Prioritizes Implementation

The university specifically identifies students who are already in the implementation phase and impacting their communities as ideal candidates.

The Stipend Is Conditional

The $2,000 stipend is provided upon successful completion of the fellowship.

There Is a Weekly Time Commitment

Selected fellows must work 8 hours per week at the Do Good Accelerator.

The Program Is Eight Weeks

The Fall 2026 cohort begins on September 28, 2026, and concludes on November 20, 2026.

The Application Deadline Is September 14, 2026

Students interested in applying should submit their applications by September 14, 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the University of Maryland Accelerator Fellows Program a scholarship?

No. It is a fellowship program focused on student projects, social impact, and venture development. Although fellows receive a $2,000 stipend upon successful completion, the program also provides coaching, workshops, resources, workspace, and developmental opportunities.

How much is the stipend?

Selected fellows receive a $2,000 stipend upon successful completion of the fellowship.

How long is the program?

The Fall 2026 program lasts eight weeks.

How many hours per week are required?

Fellows are required to work 8 hours per week at the Do Good Accelerator.

Who can apply?

The program is open to all current University of Maryland, College Park students.

Do I need to be in a particular major?

No particular academic major is specified in the provided announcement.

Is there a minimum GPA?

The announcement does not state a minimum GPA requirement.

Can international students apply?

The announcement does not impose a nationality restriction, but applicants must be current University of Maryland, College Park students. Therefore, international students who meet that student-status requirement may potentially apply.

Can someone who is not a UMD student apply?

Based on the stated eligibility criteria, no. The program is specifically open to current University of Maryland, College Park students.

Does my project have to be fully developed?

Not necessarily. The program supports students who are exploring, testing, or scaling projects. However, the university states that the ideal student is in the implementation phase and currently impacting the community.

When does the Fall 2026 program begin?

The program begins on September 28, 2026.

When does it end?

The Fall 2026 program ends on November 20, 2026.

When is the application deadline?

The application closes on September 14, 2026.

Conclusion

The University of Maryland Do Good Accelerator Fellows Program offers current University of Maryland, College Park students an opportunity to turn ongoing social impact work into stronger, more developed, and potentially more scalable initiatives.

With a $2,000 stipend, one-on-one coaching, workshops, webinars, panel discussions, community activities, workspace, and dedicated project-development time, the program provides more than financial assistance. It creates a structured environment in which students can work directly on their initiatives while learning from coaches, resources, and fellow student changemakers.

The opportunity is particularly relevant for students who have moved beyond the idea stage and are already implementing a project or social venture that is creating community impact.

For eligible students, the September 14, 2026 deadline is the key date to remember. Those selected will begin the eight-week Fall 2026 program on September 28, 2026, and complete it on November 20, 2026.

Students who are currently enrolled at UMD College Park and have a project they are actively developing should consider using this opportunity to gain structured support, strengthen their initiative, expand their skills, and increase their social impact.
